item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The global debt crisis is set to get even worse: The US fiscal deficit is projected to widen to -6....
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The global debt crisis is set to get even worse:
The US fiscal deficit is projected to widen to -6.1% of GDP in 2027, its largest since 2012, excluding the pandemic years of 2020 and 2021.
This will be the biggest deficit as a % of GDP among the 5 major developed economies, including the UK, Germany, France, and Japan.
Furthermore, Germany's deficit is expected to widen from -2.7% of GDP in 2025 to -4.1% in 2027, its largest since 2010, excluding the 2020 pandemic.
Japan's fiscal deficit is estimated to more than triple, from -0.7% to -2.5% of GDP, its largest since 2022.
The UK is the only economy expected to improve its fiscal position, with its deficit narrowing from -4.3% in 2025, to -3.1% of GDP next year, while France's budget gap is projected to widen to -5.2%.
Deficit spending is only accelerating.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US consumer stocks are struggling: The Equal-Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF, $RSPD, is down -8.0...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US consumer stocks are struggling:
The Equal-Weight Consumer Discretionary ETF, $RSPD, is down -8.0% so far in 2026, to near its lowest level since June 2025.
At the same time, the S&P 500 is up +13.9%, and is just 0.3% below its all-time high.
This leaves a massive 22-percentage-point gap in year-to-date performance.
Consumer discretionary stocks are under pressure amid weakening demand, particularly for purchases such as autos, furniture, and home-improvement goods.
At the same time, rising oil prices, elevated inflation, and rising borrowing costs are squeezing household budgets..
As a result, earnings in the Consumer Discretionary and Consumer Staples sectors are expected to decline for the first time since the end of 2024.
Is the consumer running out of money?

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US ETF industry is rapidly expanding: In total, nearly 1,100 ETFs have launched so far in 2026,...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US ETF industry is rapidly expanding:
In total, nearly 1,100 ETFs have launched so far in 2026, up +43% year-over-year.
Leveraged ETFs as a % of total ETFs launched so far in 2026 is up to a record 31.2%.
This percentage has more than quadrupled over the last 3 years.
Furthermore, 48 thematic ETFs were launched in Q3 and 46 in Q2, more than double the previous quarterly record set in Q4 2025.
Thematic ETFs provide investors with targeted exposure to specific trends, industries, technologies, or investment themes such as AI, rather than broad-market indexes.
The ETF market is becoming more specialized and leveraged.

item.description:
JUST IN: 🇺🇸 Trump administration official ordered regulators to withdraw insider trading referral involving billions in suspicious trades before President Trump's Iran announcement, Bloomberg reports.
On March 23, traders placed billions of dollars in bets that oil prices would fall and stocks would surge, just 15 minutes before Trump announced on Truth Social that he would no longer move forward with attacking Iranian infrastructure.
After the announcement, oil prices crashed 14%, while US & European stock markets surged 4%.
The CFTC identified suspicious trading patterns and referred the activity to its enforcement division.
Mel Gunewardena, a senior adviser to Trump-appointed CFTC Chairman Michael Selig, reportedly ordered investigators to retract their referral.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: 14.5% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in September, the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: 14.5% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in September, the highest rate for any September on record.
The only higher readings occurred during the pandemic shock in March and April 2020.
By comparison, between 2017 and 2019, this metric never exceeded 12.0%.
Jacksonville posted the highest cancellation rate last month, at 19.9%, followed by Tampa at 18.8%, Las Vegas at 18.6%, and San Antonio at 18.5%.
In September, home sellers outnumbered buyers by ~63%, the widest gap on record.
US homebuyers are canceling deals at a historic pace.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Shocking stat of the day: The combined wealth of the world’s tech billionaires surged +$845 billion...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Shocking stat of the day:
The combined wealth of the world’s tech billionaires surged +$845 billion in the first 9 months of 2026, the largest increase for this period of the year on record.
This brings the group's combined wealth to a record $4.6 trillion, accounting for 36% of the total wealth tracked by the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.
This is despite tech billionaires representing only ~20% of all members in the index.
For perspective, billionaires outside the technology sector lost a combined -$62 billion over the same period.
Fortunes in the consumer sector fell by -$279 billion, while those in communications declined by -$92 billion.
Americans accounted for 94% of the Bloomberg Billionaires Index's total net wealth gains in the first 9 months of 2026.
As a result, all 10 of the world's richest people have been American since September 10th, the first such occurrence since data began in 2012.
The AI boom is generating unprecedented wealth at the top.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investor demand for trading outside of regular market hours is skyrocketing. In fact, the majority...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investor demand for trading outside of regular market hours is skyrocketing.
In fact, the majority of trading volume in tokenized equities is now occurring OUTSIDE of regular market hours.
BNB Chain has become the first blockchain with over 70% of its tokenized equity trading volume occurring outside of regular market hours.
On Solana, 63% of tokenized equity trading volume is now occurring outside of regular market hours.
Amid this trend, Jupiter, the largest trading platform on Solana, reported +50% month-over-month growth in tokenized asset trading volumes.
As a result, the total circulating supply of tokenized equities has surged to a record $3.3 billion.
Markets are officially becoming 24/7.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: We are witnessing a historic shift. The annual spread between the S&P 500's earnings yield and the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
We are witnessing a historic shift.
The annual spread between the S&P 500's earnings yield and the 10Y Note yield is down to -1.5 percentage points, its lowest since 2009.
Since 2022, this yield difference has fallen -440 basis points, its largest 5-year decline since the 1970s.
As a result, the S&P 500's equity risk premium is on track to post its 3rd consecutive negative annual reading, the longest streak since 2002.
This suggests that, on a yield basis, theoretically less risky 10Y Treasuries are now more attractive than the S&P 500.
In other words, investors are receiving a higher yield from Treasuries than from the S&P 500, despite the additional risk of owning stocks.
Historically, a negative equity risk premium has been associated with strong risk appetite and stretched equity valuations.
We expect an eventful Q4 ahead.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US bull market is entering its 5th year.
Since the October 2022 low, the S&P 500 has rallied +118%, outpacing the average bull market since WWII.
This is also the 3rd-largest gain among bull markets at their 4th anniversary.
Over this period, the index has returned +21.6% in Year 1, +33.7% in Year 2, +12.7% in Year 3, and +19.4% in Year 4.
The average S&P 500 bull market's return since WWII has been +20.8% in Year 5, the 2nd-strongest 12-month performance after +39.1% in Year 1.
Of the 13 previous bull markets, only 6 lasted long enough to reach this stage.
If history is any guide, the market is heading for another year of strong gains.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US stock market has never been this fragmented: The 52-week correlation between the equal-weigh...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US stock market has never been this fragmented:
The 52-week correlation between the equal-weighted S&P 500 and the S&P 500 index is down to 0.67, its lowest level on record.
This measures how closely the performance of the equal-weighted S&P 500 tracks the cap-weighted index, with a lower reading indicating a growing gap between the broader market and mega-cap stocks.
The correlation has declined -0.25 points since August 2025.
By comparison, before the 2020 pandemic, this figure remained between 0.95 and 0.99 for nearly 15 years.
To put this into perspective, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, this metric never declined below 0.85.
The S&P 500 is more concentrated than ever.

Moving out now takes a job, and often a parent's wallet.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META LAUNCHES MUSE WONDER FOR PERSONAL AI AGENTS AND CODING Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse W...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META LAUNCHES MUSE WONDER FOR PERSONAL AI AGENTS AND CODING
Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, calling them its most capable models yet. Both were trained at its gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center.
The series combines Active Memory, which carries relevant context across conversations, with Active Focus, designed to keep agents working through complex tasks, trying alternative approaches and checking with users before important actions.
The models target personal assistance and professional workflows, including software development and tasks involving legal, financial and health information. Meta reports state-of-the-art results across benchmarks for agents, memory and coding.
For developers, the coding capabilities focus on sustained work across projects: tracking requirements, changing multiple parts of a codebase, testing results and making revisions.
Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code. Muse Wonder Full is available to Muse Code subscribers.
Muse Wonder will also roll out to the Muse app, starting with subscribers, and power artifact generation and other tasks requiring more advanced capabilities.
Meta says the models include stronger safeguards for private information, malicious instructions and misuse. A fuller safety report is expected later. https://x.com/finkd/status/2109689307288240154/video/1
item.content:encoded:
$META LAUNCHES MUSE WONDER FOR PERSONAL AI AGENTS AND CODING

Meta introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, calling them its most capable models yet. Both were trained at its gigawatt-scale Prometheus data center.

The series combines Active Memory, which carries relevant context across conversations, with Active Focus, designed to keep agents working through complex tasks, trying alternative approaches and checking with users before important actions.

The models target personal assistance and professional workflows, including software development and tasks involving legal, financial and health information. Meta reports state-of-the-art results across benchmarks for agents, memory and coding.

For developers, the coding capabilities focus on sustained work across projects: tracking requirements, changing multiple parts of a codebase, testing results and making revisions.

Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code. Muse Wonder Full is available to Muse Code subscribers.

Muse Wonder will also roll out to the Muse app, starting with subscribers, and power artifact generation and other tasks requiring more advanced capabilities.

Meta says the models include stronger safeguards for private information, malicious instructions and misuse. A fuller safety report is expected later. https://x.com/finkd/status/2109689307288240154/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The global rate hike cycle is here. 15 of the 33 major central banks, or 45%, have raised interest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The global rate hike cycle is here.
15 of the 33 major central banks, or 45%, have raised interest rates over the last 6 months, the largest proportion since 2023.
This figure is now approaching the ~55%, recorded in 2018 and 2011.
By comparison, the proportion peaked at ~95% in 2022, following post-pandemic stimulus and the resulting surge in global inflation.
In total, 54 central banks have hiked rates so far in 2026.
This also marks the first time since September 2023 that more central banks have hiked than cut rates over a rolling 3-month period.
"Higher for longer" is back.

item.title: @wallstengine: $NVDA OPENS VERA RUBIN RACK DESIGNS, EXPANDS AI NETWORKING WITH META, GOOGLE AND CISCO NVIDIA annou...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$NVDA OPENS VERA RUBIN RACK DESIGNS, EXPANDS AI NETWORKING WITH META, GOOGLE AND CISCO
NVIDIA announced new partnerships and open infrastructure contributions at the OCP Global Summit, covering rack designs, networking, software and power systems for next-generation AI data centers.
The company contributed key Vera Rubin rack and compute tray designs through its MGX architecture. The updated MGX 1.2 specification supports racks up to 250kW, with standardized power connections, liquid cooling and fanless compute trays.
$META is adopting NVIDIA’s Spectrum-6 Ethernet switches, which deliver 102.4Tb/s of switching capacity. Combined with Spectrum-X Multiplane technology, the architecture is designed to connect more than 100,000 GPUs with fewer switch layers. Traffic is distributed across up to eight independent network paths, allowing workloads to keep running if a component fails.
Cisco $CSCO and NVIDIA announced plans for USFP, a new pluggable optical module designed for 400Gb/s-per-lane networking. The companies say it will deliver 4x the bandwidth density and approximately 1.3x the power efficiency of 200Gb/s-per-lane modules, with up to 12.8Tb/s of overall capacity in roughly the same physical footprint.
TE Connectivity and Amphenol are helping develop USFP connectors, cages and modules. The companies plan to establish an open industry specification, giving multiple suppliers a common design to build around.
Google’s Falcon Transport will be supported on future NVIDIA ConnectX-10 SuperNICs and BlueField DPUs. The collaboration enables NVIDIA and Google networking hardware to communicate over a common transport, with features for managing congestion, recovering dropped packets and protecting connections.
NVIDIA also released new open-source DSX software components for configuring networks, stress-testing GPU clusters, managing racks and preparing hardware for deployment. Its Vera CPU rack design specifically targets AI agent workloads, including tool calling, orchestration and sandboxed execution.
On power infrastructure, NVIDIA joined AMD, Google and Meta on an open data-center design specification, and Google, Meta and Microsoft on grid-resilience standards.
Separately, Visionbay introduced plans for K-1, an 800V DC AI factory platform combining NVIDIA’s reference architecture with Vertiv’s power and cooling technologies for future Vera Rubin deployments.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted +$30.7 billion in inflows in Q3 2026, their la...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Global physical gold-backed ETFs attracted +$30.7 billion in inflows in Q3 2026, their largest quarterly intake on record.
In September, inflows totaled +$10 billion, the 3rd-largest monthly inflow of 2026, following +$17.9 billion in August, the 2nd-largest monthly intake on record.
As a result, global gold ETF holdings rose +67 tonnes last month to a record 4,256 tonnes.
This surpasses the previous record of 4,176 tonnes set in February.
Year-to-date, global gold ETFs have seen +$38.5 billion in inflows, equivalent to an increase of +226 tonnes in gold holdings, with all regions recording positive demand.
UK-listed funds have attracted +$9.5 billion in inflows over the same period, overtaking China to become the largest source of country-level demand so far in 2026.
Demand for gold is extremely strong.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US seasonal hiring is off to a weak start: US-based employers announced plans to hire 90,787 worker...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US seasonal hiring is off to a weak start:
US-based employers announced plans to hire 90,787 workers in September, the weakest September total since 2011.
This marks a -23% decline from the 117,313 recorded in September 2025.
Retail led all industries last month, with 65,150 announced hires, followed by Aerospace and Defense at 5,300.
However, announced seasonal hiring is muted so far this year, with a combined 62,000 seasonal hires, compared with 100,800 announced by seasonal employers last September.
Year-to-date, US hiring plans have totaled 210,612 workers, the 2nd-lowest total for the first 9 months of the year in at least 10 years.
Retail leads all sectors with 66,557 announcements so far in 2026, followed by Technology, at 22,361, and Aerospace and Defense, at 21,841.
Hiring demand remains muted.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The gap between AI names and the rest of the market is historic: Since the start of 2024, a basket...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The gap between AI names and the rest of the market is historic:
Since the start of 2024, a basket of 42 AI stocks has generated 67% of the S&P 500's price return.
In other words, those names have contributed +22 percentage points to the index’s +33% gain over this period.
By comparison, the remaining 458 stocks have added +11 percentage points.
Additionally, those 42 AI stocks have accounted for 58% of the S&P 500's earnings growth and 81% of CapEx and R&D growth since the start of 2024.
The rest of the index has therefore contributed just 20% of total CapEx and R&D growth over the same period.
Meanwhile, just 29% of stocks have outperformed the S&P 500 over the last 3 years, close to the ~25% low recorded during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.
AI is all that matters.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US families are falling behind on debt payments. The percentage of families reporting overdue loan...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US families are falling behind on debt payments.
The percentage of families reporting overdue loan payments surged to 19.6% in 2025, the highest since 2010, according to the Fed data.
This marks a sharp increase from 12.2% recorded in 2022.
This also reverses the gradual improvement between 2013 and 2019, when the percentage declined by -2.6 points.
Furthermore, more than 8.0% of families reported they were at least 2 months behind on payments, up from 5.0% in 2022.
This comes despite the typical family debt load remaining unchanged since 2022, suggesting that more households are struggling to keep up with existing financial obligations.
Americans are falling behind on loan payments at a concerning pace.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The Bank of Japan's total assets declined -$98 billion in Q3 2026, to $3.95 trillion, the...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The Bank of Japan's total assets declined -$98 billion in Q3 2026, to $3.95 trillion, the lowest since Q1 2020.
Since the Q1 2024 peak, the BoJ has reduced its balance sheet by -$828 billion, or -17.4%.
As a result, the BoJ's Asset-to-GDP ratio has fallen -28 percentage points over this period, to 94%, the lowest since 2018.
Furthermore, Japanese government bond holdings fell -$90 billion in Q3, to $3.19 trillion, the lowest since Q1 2020.
Since the 2023 peak, JGB holdings have dropped -$556 billion, or -14.9%.
The BoJ also sold -$568 million in equity ETFs and J-REITs last quarter, bringing its holdings down to $233 billion, the lowest since Q3 2021.
The Bank of Japan continues to unwind its balance sheet.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: China’s industrial profit growth is losing momentum: China’s industrial profits rose +4.2% YoY in A...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
China’s industrial profit growth is losing momentum:
China’s industrial profits rose +4.2% YoY in August, the weakest YoY growth since November 2025.
This also marks the 4th consecutive monthly slowdown in growth.
Pressure is particularly visible in consumer-facing industries, where profits are falling in autos, clothing, and furniture.
Domestic demand continues to weaken, with consumption growth slowing to near zero while manufacturers, property developers, and infrastructure builders are cutting spending.
For the first 8 months of 2026, industrial profits were still up +15.7% YoY, but the gains are becoming increasingly concentrated, with the electronics industry contributing ~66% of total growth.
At the same time, raw-material industries contributed +6.2 percentage points to the overall increase, supported by higher commodity prices.
Weak domestic demand is weighing on China’s economy.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US deficit is surging despite low unemployment. The cumulative US fiscal deficit since 2020 has...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US deficit is surging despite low unemployment.
The cumulative US fiscal deficit since 2020 has surged to a massive $14.18 trillion.
Meanwhile, the 7-year average unemployment rate has fallen -0.4 percentage points, to 4.7% over the same period.
In the first 11 months of FY2026 alone, the US deficit totaled $1.97 trillion, the 3rd-largest for this period of the year in history.
When the economy is strong and unemployment is low, the government would typically keep fiscal deficits lower, reserving large-scale fiscal support for periods of economic weakness.
This time, however, the deficit is running at historically high levels despite stable unemployment.
This comes as elevated government spending and rising interest costs are keeping the deficit exceptionally large even without a recession.
Massive deficits have become a permanent feature of the US economy.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Shocking stat of the day: $241 billion worth of French corporate bonds are now trading at lower yie...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Shocking stat of the day:
$241 billion worth of French corporate bonds are now trading at lower yields than French government bonds.
This figure is up +1,621% from just $14 billion at the start of 2026.
This means ~38% of French high-grade corporate debt is now trading at lower yields than government bonds of similar maturity.
The gap between corporate and government bond yields is widening as investor concerns about France's deteriorating fiscal situation weigh on government debt.
As a result, internationally exposed companies such as L'Oreal, $OR, and TotalEnergies, $TTE, are increasingly viewed as safer alternatives to French government debt, unlike French banks, which remain more exposed to sovereign risk.
This is in stark contrast to normal economic conditions, when government bonds are traditionally viewed as the safest part of the bond market.
France's corporate bond market is increasingly being treated a safer bet than its government bonds.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The cost of consumer credit is rising. The average interest rate on a US credit card rose +0.2 perc...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The cost of consumer credit is rising.
The average interest rate on a US credit card rose +0.2 percentage points in August, to 22.36%, its highest level in 12 months.
This is now only 1.0 percentage point below the record 23.37% set in August 2024.
Since 2021, the average credit card interest rate has surged +6.5 percentage points.
By comparison, the 5-year average before the 2020 pandemic was 14.94%.
Meanwhile, the average interest rate on a 5-year new car loan rose +0.4 percentage points in August, to 7.54%, its highest since August 2025.
This is 3.5 percentage points above pre-pandemic levels, but 0.9 percentage points below its all-time high of 8.4%, recorded in August 2024.
Consumer borrowing has rarely been this expensive.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI will become one of the largest spending categories in the US economy: AI services are projected...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI will become one of the largest spending categories in the US economy:
AI services are projected to account for a record 8.8% of US GDP in 2032.
This estimate shows how much businesses and consumers are expected to spend per year on the services of AI companies.
This also implies AI companies would generate ~$3.5 trillion in annual revenue by 2032.
By comparison, US consumer spending on food accounts for a similar 9.1% of GDP.
This figure would also be ~72% higher than energy, at 5.1% of GDP, and twice the size of construction as well as computers and software, both at 4.4%.
It would also be nearly 3x defense, at 2.8%, and more than 7x communications and internet, at 1.2% of GDP.
The only category where spending is significantly larger is health, at 18% of GDP.
The scale of the AI revolution is unlike anything seen before.
item.content:encoded:
AI will become one of the largest spending categories in the US economy:

AI services are projected to account for a record 8.8% of US GDP in 2032.

This estimate shows how much businesses and consumers are expected to spend per year on the services of AI companies.

This also implies AI companies would generate ~$3.5 trillion in annual revenue by 2032.

By comparison, US consumer spending on food accounts for a similar 9.1% of GDP.

This figure would also be ~72% higher than energy, at 5.1% of GDP, and twice the size of construction as well as computers and software, both at 4.4%.

It would also be nearly 3x defense, at 2.8%, and more than 7x communications and internet, at 1.2% of GDP.

The only category where spending is significantly larger is health, at 18% of GDP.

The scale of the AI revolution is unlike anything seen before.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: China’s central bank officially bought +23 tonnes of gold in September, its largest month...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: China’s central bank officially bought +23 tonnes of gold in September, its largest monthly purchase since September 2023.
This follows +20 tonnes purchased in both August and July, and marks its 23rd consecutive monthly gold purchase.
So far in 2026, China has officially acquired +103 tonnes of gold, raising total holdings to a record 2,410 tonnes.
China is now the world’s 5th-largest gold holder, following the US, Germany, Italy, and France.
At this pace, it could surpass Italy and France as early as this year, which hold 2,452 tonnes and 2,437 tonnes, respectively.
China is aggressively buying the dip in gold.

The AI trade is leaving the rest of the market far behind.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Pine Computer has introduced a cloud computer built for AI agents, with an operating system that sends structured app data and live updates directly to models.
In Pine’s SaaS-Bench v1.1 comparison, GPT-5.6 Luna achieved a 78.3% checkpoint score versus 71.1% for GPT-5.6 Sol + Codex, at approximately 1/20 the model-token cost.
Developers can use its SDK to automate spreadsheet analysis, navigate websites without APIs and run tasks across apps and files in parallel.
Users can take over for logins or approvals, then return control to AI. Sign-ins and learned skills carry over between sessions.
The benchmark measures progress through tasks, not full-task completion, and the cost comparison excludes infrastructure.
@PineAIAssistant is currently available through an invite-only private beta.

item.title: @wallstengine: Sabi has raised $50M to build a cap designed to turn brain signals into prompts for AI, without a b...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Sabi has raised $50M to build a cap designed to turn brain signals into prompts for AI, without a brain implant.
Backers include Khosla Ventures, Accel, Initialized, DST Global and Kevin Weil.
The company says its low-power, non-contact sensors can capture neural signals through hair. Founder Rahul Chhabra credits TSMC with helping fabricate its custom chip.
The design also combines neural sensing with a camera, microphone and voice AI, aiming to connect a user’s intent with context from their surroundings.
Sabi plans to preview the cap at CES 2027 and is accepting applications for invite-only early access.

However, since the previous record, only 4 sectors have posted positive returns.
Technology led at+6.8%, followed by Energy at +4.4%, Communication Services at +1.2%, and Healthcare at +0.6%.
Therefore, only 3 sectors have outperformed the S&P 500 over this period.
On the other hand, Industrials, Real Estate, and Financials have lagged the most, falling -9.5%, -8.0%, and -7.2%, respectively.
Technology and Energy stocks are carrying the market.

As a precaution, and pending the results of our investigation, we have asked CryptoBilis to pause all sales and shipments of Ledger devices.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Total consumer credit rose +$8.3 billion in August, to a record $5.19 trillion. This mark...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Total consumer credit rose +$8.3 billion in August, to a record $5.19 trillion.
This marks the 14th consecutive monthly increase, totalling +$154 billion.
Since the start of 2022, consumer credit has risen +$684 billion.
Non-revolving credit, covering auto and student loans, rose +$13.1 billion in August, to $3.84 trillion, an all-time high.
Meanwhile, revolving credit, which includes credit cards, fell -$4.8 billion, to $1.35 trillion, its 4th-highest level on record.
US consumers are still borrowing.

item.title: @wallstengine: JENSEN HUANG: FROM A 9-YEAR-OLD IMMIGRANT TO AMERICA’S HIGHEST SCIENCE HONOR Nvidia co-founder Jens...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
JENSEN HUANG: FROM A 9-YEAR-OLD IMMIGRANT TO AMERICA’S HIGHEST SCIENCE HONOR
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang received the National Medal of Science today, recognizing his contributions to computing and AI.
His parents were also there to share the moment.
Born in Taiwan, Huang was just nine when his parents sent him and his brother to live with an uncle in the United States. The family later reunited in Oregon.
At 15, he worked at Denny’s washing dishes, clearing tables and serving customers. He went on to earn electrical engineering degrees from Oregon State and Stanford.
In 1993, he co-founded NVIDIA with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, developing their early plans over meetings at a Denny’s. Their starting idea was to bring better 3D graphics to personal computers.
Thirty-three years later, Huang is being honored for helping turn graphics processors into a foundation for scientific computing and artificial intelligence.
There’s something special about this beyond the company or the medal: the parents who sent their son across the world getting to stand beside him for a moment like this.

item.title: @wallstengine: SPACEX SIGNS SPECTRUM DEAL TO MAKE STARLINK A MAJOR U.S. MOBILE CARRIER $SPCX has agreed to acquire...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
SPACEX SIGNS SPECTRUM DEAL TO MAKE STARLINK A MAJOR U.S. MOBILE CARRIER
$SPCX has agreed to acquire Grain Management’s nationwide portfolio of 800 MHz low-band spectrum licenses, a move the company says will pave the way for Starlink to become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.
Elon Musk called it “the last critical piece of the spectrum puzzle needed for SpaceX to provide complete phone coverage in America.”
The plan is to combine satellites with a ground-based mobile network. The low-band airwaves would complement Starlink’s 2 GHz spectrum, helping improve indoor coverage and extend service into areas with weak or nonexistent cellular reception. That would put Starlink in more direct competition with AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile.
Separately, the FCC approved a new constellation of 15,000 SpaceX satellites this week for direct-to-device mobile services, another step toward expanding Starlink’s ability to connect directly to phones.
The spectrum acquisition still requires FCC approval and other customary closing conditions. Financial terms were not disclosed.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Americans are worried about inflation. US consumer median 1-year ahead inflation expectations jumpe...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Americans are worried about inflation.
US consumer median 1-year ahead inflation expectations jumped +0.3 percentage points in September, to 3.9%, their highest level since May 2023.
This figure has risen +0.9 percentage points since February.
Over the next year, consumers expect gasoline prices to increase +4.8%, food prices to rise +5.5%, medical costs to surge +9.2%, the price of a college education to jump +7.5%, and rent prices to rise +6.8%.
1-year inflation expectations have now been at or above 3.0% for 22 consecutive months.
Meanwhile, 3-year inflation expectations rose +0.1 percentage point last month, to 3.3%, the highest level since June 2022.
Consumers are bracing for a prolonged period of higher prices.

item.title: @Hedgeye: McCullough: Stop Measuring Yourself Against Warren Buffett 🔊 "You are not Warren Buffett, and you...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
McCullough: Stop Measuring Yourself Against Warren Buffett
🔊
"You are not Warren Buffett, and you actually want to have risk management at the core, quantitative strategies at the core," @KeithMcCullough said at the Hedgeye Investing Summit.
Hedgeye Portfolio Manager Sam Rahman @Hedgeye_HGRO says very few investors can hold positions the way Buffett has.
"Very, very few people have the luxury to have that kind of duration of the capital," Rahman says.
"Buffett owns his duration because he owned the capital."
Rahman says his own long-term view runs one to three years, with many short-term moves to manage along the way.
"That doesn't mean you buy and hold and you sit there for three years and pray that it's going to work out."
McCullough describes the alternative as a top-down macro view like Stan Druckenmiller's combined with stock picking. "One bear market will convince you."
item.content:encoded:
McCullough: Stop Measuring Yourself Against Warren Buffett

🔊

"You are not Warren Buffett, and you actually want to have risk management at the core, quantitative strategies at the core," @KeithMcCullough said at the Hedgeye Investing Summit.

Hedgeye Portfolio Manager Sam Rahman @Hedgeye_HGRO says very few investors can hold positions the way Buffett has.

"Very, very few people have the luxury to have that kind of duration of the capital," Rahman says.

"Buffett owns his duration because he owned the capital."

Rahman says his own long-term view runs one to three years, with many short-term moves to manage along the way.

"That doesn't mean you buy and hold and you sit there for three years and pray that it's going to work out."

McCullough describes the alternative as a top-down macro view like Stan Druckenmiller's combined with stock picking. "One bear market will convince you."

item.title: @wallstengine: SUI BASECAMP 2026: HERE’S EVERYTHING ANNOUNCED, FROM SAMSUNG WALLET TO A 40.6M TPS DEMO Sui wrapped...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
SUI BASECAMP 2026:
HERE’S EVERYTHING ANNOUNCED, FROM SAMSUNG WALLET TO A 40.6M TPS DEMO
Sui wrapped up its two-day Basecamp event in Singapore with major announcements across payments, AI, Bitcoin finance and blockchain infrastructure.
Samsung Wallet is integrating USDC on Sui, potentially reaching 82M U.S. Galaxy devices, with zero network fees on supported transfers.
Sui demonstrated 40.6M TPS through programmable offchain tunnels that settle to mainnet, surpassing its previous test record of roughly 6.1M.
Hashi’s Bitcoin finance mainnet begins rolling out this month with over $500M in committed capital and Anchorage Digital joining as a launch partner.
On the AI side, Alibaba Cloud announced a collaboration on agent payments, while Mysten Labs and Google Cloud introduced Verifiable Agent Arbiter to help enterprises verify that AI agents act within authorized limits.
Other announcements included Walrus Console for AI app data, Sui Agent Pass, Sui Threat Intelligence, and Circle’s CCTP V2 going live.
The event also featured live AI demonstrations and a trading competition on Hudi, with @TraderMayne taking the top spot. https://x.com/SuiNetwork/status/2108149753553015088/video/1

item.title: @Hedgeye: Leyla Kunimoto @LeylaKuni, Founder of Accredited Investor Insights, says private credit valuations...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Leyla Kunimoto @LeylaKuni, Founder of Accredited Investor Insights, says private credit valuations rest on numbers investors can’t verify.
Most private loans are Level 3 assets with no market price, so funds value them using their own models.
“Valuations are determined based on internal models and nobody knows what inputs go into internal models,” Kunimoto told Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough at the Hedgeye Investing Summit.
She points to the loan behind Medallia, a software company taken private by a large private equity firm and financed by a group of private credit managers.
After the loan became impaired, she says, “marks on that one loan were diverging by a good margin between the different people who held it.”
“How can I have faith in those marks at all,” Kunimoto says, if “on the very same thing, our marks are so very different.”

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI'S ANNUALIZED REVENUE NEARS $50B, BELOW EARLIER $70B REPORTS: FT OpenAI recently told investo...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI'S ANNUALIZED REVENUE NEARS $50B, BELOW EARLIER $70B REPORTS: FT
OpenAI recently told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50B at the end of September, roughly $20B below the figure widely reported last month.
The discrepancy reportedly stems from differences in how OpenAI and Anthropic calculate revenue. Anthropic includes sales through cloud partners such as AWS and Google Cloud, while OpenAI does not.
Investors had attempted to adjust OpenAI's figures to make them comparable with Anthropic's, contributing to the previously reported $70B estimate.
OpenAI declined to comment.
Source: Financial Times.
item.content:encoded:
OPENAI'S ANNUALIZED REVENUE NEARS $50B, BELOW EARLIER $70B REPORTS: FT

OpenAI recently told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50B at the end of September, roughly $20B below the figure widely reported last month.

The discrepancy reportedly stems from differences in how OpenAI and Anthropic calculate revenue. Anthropic includes sales through cloud partners such as AWS and Google Cloud, while OpenAI does not.

Investors had attempted to adjust OpenAI's figures to make them comparable with Anthropic's, contributing to the previously reported $70B estimate.

OpenAI declined to comment.

Source: Financial Times.

item.title: @WatcherGuru: JUST IN: 🇺🇸 CFTC says "America is no longer sitting back while crypto moves overseas, and other c...
item.dc:creator: @WatcherGuru
item.description:
JUST IN: 🇺🇸 CFTC says "America is no longer sitting back while crypto moves overseas, and other countries set the standard."
"America leading the way."
Over the past month, the CFTC has taken the following actions after Congress failed to pass the Clarity Act:
• CFTC Chair Mike Selig orders staff to move forward with a formal crypto market structure framework.
• CFTC allows developers to create passive derivatives software, including for crypto, without requiring broker registration.
• CFTC launches files new rulemaking to establish regulatory oversight of crypto trading and transactions.
• CFTC Chair Mike Selig says the agency is preparing for a future built around "onchain systems, mass tokenization, 24/7 trading, and agentic finance."
• CFTC releases updated regulatory guidance addressing crypto, tokenized assets, and blockchain-based technologies.
• CFTC proposes its first set of rules to regulate the US crypto industry.
• CFTC advances new investor protection measures aimed at preventing fraud, manipulation, and abuse in crypto markets.
• CFTC says it will establish clear crypto regulations regardless of whether Congress passes legislation.
item.content:encoded:
JUST IN: 🇺🇸 CFTC says "America is no longer sitting back while crypto moves overseas, and other countries set the standard."

"America leading the way."

Over the past month, the CFTC has taken the following actions after Congress failed to pass the Clarity Act:

• CFTC Chair Mike Selig orders staff to move forward with a formal crypto market structure framework.

• CFTC allows developers to create passive derivatives software, including for crypto, without requiring broker registration.

• CFTC launches files new rulemaking to establish regulatory oversight of crypto trading and transactions.

• CFTC Chair Mike Selig says the agency is preparing for a future built around "onchain systems, mass tokenization, 24/7 trading, and agentic finance."

• CFTC releases updated regulatory guidance addressing crypto, tokenized assets, and blockchain-based technologies.

• CFTC proposes its first set of rules to regulate the US crypto industry.

• CFTC advances new investor protection measures aimed at preventing fraud, manipulation, and abuse in crypto markets.

• CFTC says it will establish clear crypto regulations regardless of whether Congress passes legislation.

Cogent has launched Attack Path Analysis, an AI security tool designed to map how attackers could reach a company’s most sensitive systems and data.
It connects signals across cloud infrastructure, identity systems and code to identify chains of vulnerabilities, exposed credentials and excessive permissions.
It checks the evidence behind each step and recommends changes that could break several attack routes at once, such as removing a shared permission.
The goal is to help security teams prioritize fixes based on what an attacker could actually reach. https://x.com/vineete_5/status/2108205982409261181/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Retail investors are extremely bullish: Allocation to stocks among retail investors in the AAII sur...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Retail investors are extremely bullish:
Allocation to stocks among retail investors in the AAII survey rose +0.7 percentage points in September, to 71.8%, the highest level since December 2017.
This also marks its 2nd-highest reading since July 2000.
Since April, this figure has risen +3.3 percentage points, its largest 5-month increase since October 2025.
To put this into perspective, average retail exposure to stocks since 1987 is 71.8%.
Meanwhile, allocation to cash fell -1.0 percentage point last month to 13.3%, its lowest since December 2017.
At the same time, allocation to bonds rose +0.3 percentage points, to 14.9%, remaining below its average of 15.9% since 1987.
Appetite for risk among retail investors is through the roof.

item.title: @wallstengine: BROADCOM SEEKS $50B+ IN FINANCING FOR OPENAI’S CUSTOM AI CHIPS: WSJ Apollo and Blackstone are among...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
BROADCOM SEEKS $50B+ IN FINANCING FOR OPENAI’S CUSTOM AI CHIPS: WSJ
Apollo and Blackstone are among the lenders $AVGO has approached about participating.
The financing could cover several gigawatts of chip capacity, with a deal expected before year-end. Discussions remain early, and the amount could change.
OpenAI’s chip program is internally known as “Nexus,” with its first two generations named “Jalapeño” and “Serrano.”
The companies previously announced a partnership to develop 10 GW of custom AI chips using Broadcom’s networking technology, with deployments planned from the second half of 2026 through 2029.
The financing push comes as OpenAI looks to own more of its computing infrastructure to lower costs and reduce reliance on cloud providers.
Source: WSJ.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The "AI Big 10" now accounts for a record 42% of US stock market cap. This includes Magni...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The "AI Big 10" now accounts for a record 42% of US stock market cap.
This includes Magnificent 7 stocks as well as Broadcom, $AVGO, AMD, $AMD, and Micron, $MU.
This figure has more than doubled since the 2022 bear market low.
By comparison, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, the Technology, Media & Telecom (TMT) sector peaked at 41%, while the Nifty Fifty peaked at 40% in the 1970s.
Furthermore, Japan’s equity market bubble in the 1980s peaked at 44%.
In the past, only railroad stocks have significantly exceeded this concentration, accounting for 63% of US market cap at their highest point in the 1900s.
The dominance of Big Tech is extraordinary.

This follows +23 tonnes in July and +52 tonnes in June.
China again led demand, adding +20 tonnes and bringing its year-to-date purchases to +80 tonnes.
China’s official gold reserves have now risen to a record 2,387 tonnes, or 9% of its total FX reserves.
Furthermore, Poland bought +8 tonnes, lifting its year-to-date purchases to +98 tonnes and total gold reserves to a record 648 tonnes.
So far in 2026, central banks have acquired +170 tonnes of gold.
Central banks continue to aggressively accumulate gold.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Since the start of 2025, US jobs numbers have now been revised down in 16 out of 20 month...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Since the start of 2025, US jobs numbers have now been revised down in 16 out of 20 months by a total of -793,000 jobs.
This means that, on average, -39,650 jobs have been revised out of previously reported data each month during this period.
The most recent August and July jobs numbers were revised down by a total of -60,000.
Revisions to nonfarm payrolls have consistently occurred since the start of 2023.
If we apply this average to the +29,000 jobs add in September's report, it would imply a -10,650 contraction in nonfarm payrolls last month.
This would also mark their 3rd monthly decline of 2026, following a -156,000 drop in February and -10,000 in July.
What is happening here?

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Executives in the Financials sector are turning cautious: The unique seller/buyer ratio for Financi...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Executives in the Financials sector are turning cautious:
The unique seller/buyer ratio for Financials stood at 2.10x above its long-term average in Q3 2026, the highest reading across all major sectors.
This ratio compares the number of individual insiders who sold shares with the number who bought, regardless of how many times they sold.
The number of financial executives buying their own stocks in the sector fell to its lowest level in almost 23 years, while the number of sellers was not unusually high.
Energy and Technology followed, with ratios of 1.30x and 1.24x, respectively.
At the same time, the broader market seller/buyer ratio stood at 1.20x its long-term average last quarter, or 20% above the historical norm.
On the other hand, Consumer Staples had the lowest reading at just 0.50x, followed by Utilities at 0.55x and Materials at 0.57x.
Insider confidence is fading across key market sectors.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The employment downturn in the US Information sector is intensifying: Information employment fell a...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The employment downturn in the US Information sector is intensifying:
Information employment fell another -10,000 jobs in September, to 2.739 million, the lowest since December 2020.
Excluding the 2020 pandemic drop, this is the lowest level since December 2014.
In total, the Information industry has shed -376,000 jobs, or -12.1%, since the November 2022 peak.
To put this into perspective, during the 2001 recession and its aftermath, Information employment fell -568,000 jobs, or -15.3%, from March 2001 to December 2003.
The Information sector is losing jobs at a crisis pace.

Monid has raised $7.7M, led by Long Journey Ventures, with participation from Madrona, 1984 Ventures, Essence VC and Pioneer Fund.

item.title: @wallstengine: AgentMail has launched AgentID, a “Sign in with Google” equivalent for AI agents that lets them sig...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
AgentMail has launched AgentID, a “Sign in with Google” equivalent for AI agents that lets them sign into apps with their own verified email identity instead of borrowing their owner’s account.
Each agent is linked to a human owner, allowing apps to recognize when multiple agents belong to the same person, set limits per customer and contact someone about billing or abuse.
AgentID uses the OpenID Connect standard and works with existing login platforms including Clerk, Auth0 and Supabase. It’s free for apps to add, while agents need an AgentMail inbox.
AgentMail says 10 million agents already use its platform. The goal is to let apps accept those agents as users while knowing who is behind them, rather than blocking them outright. https://x.com/haakamaujla/status/2107520017122443267/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Short interest in the Russell 2000 index is up to 8.0% of shares outstanding, the highest...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Short interest in the Russell 2000 index is up to 8.0% of shares outstanding, the highest since at least 2019.
Since the start of 2025, this percentage has nearly doubled.
By comparison, before the 2022 bear market, short interest in small-cap stocks was ~3.5%.
This comes after the S&P 500 outperformed the Russell 2000 in Q3 2026 by 9.6 percentage points, its largest outperformance since Q1 2020.
Meanwhile, short interest in the S&P 500 ETF, $SPY, stands at ~9.0% of shares outstanding, below the 10.0% average seen in 2024-2025 and far below the 15.0% average between 2020 and 2023.
Are small caps set for a short squeeze?

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Diversification is dying. For every $1 invested in the S&P 500, ~41 cents now goes to just the 10 l...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Diversification is dying.
For every $1 invested in the S&P 500, ~41 cents now goes to just the 10 largest stocks.
Nvidia, $NVDA, alone accounts for 8 cents, followed by Apple, $AAPL, at 7 cents, Microsoft, $MSFT, and Alphabet, $GOOGL, at 6 cents each, and Amazon, $AMZN, at 4 cents.
The next 5 mega-cap names, Broadcom, $AVGO, Meta, $META, Tesla, $TSLA, Micron, $MU, and AMD, $AMD, represent another 10 cents combined.
By comparison, the next 10 largest firms account for just 10 cents combined.
The top 10 stocks now represent almost 2x the allocation of 402 other companies in the index, which together account for just 23 cents of every $1.
Big Tech effectively is the market.

AMPERSAND RAISES $15M TO HELP AI AGENTS WORK INSIDE ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE
Ampersand has raised a $15M Series A led by Bessemer, bringing total funding to $20M, as it makes its integration platform generally available.
The company helps AI agents connect to systems like Salesforce, NetSuite, SAP and Workday, where custom fields, permissions and workflows can make each customer deployment a separate engineering project.
The new funding will support broader ERP coverage, agentic integration infrastructure and more forward-deployed expertise.
Ampersand is also launching Andi, its AI integration agent, in beta after spending three years building alongside customers including 11x, Orb and Square.

This also marks +247% growth compared to levels seen in October 2025.
Continued adoption of stablecoins as a payment rail and the push toward cross-border transaction efficiency are behind the surge in volume.
Furthermore, QR-code based payments for crypto cards are seeing robust growth.
This has fueled +55% quarter-over-quarter growth in activated cards on Jupiter Spend, one of the largest onchain card providers, particularly due to demand for QR payments.
Crypto cards are the next phase of crypto adoption.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Nvidia, $NVDA, now accounts for 5.21% of the MSCI All Country World Index (ACWI), near th...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Nvidia, $NVDA, now accounts for 5.21% of the MSCI All Country World Index (ACWI), near the highest level on record.
The ACWI Index covers ~85% of global equity markets, including large and mid-cap stocks across 23 developed and 24 emerging markets.
This figure has more than doubled since 2024.
Nvidia’s weight is now even larger than Japan’s weight of 5.16%, the world’s 3rd-largest stock market.
Its contribution to the index is also more than twice that of Germany’s 1.79%, France’s 1.93%, and China’s 2.31%
By comparison, the UK and Canada represent 2.95% and 2.91%, respectively.
Nvidia is in a league of its own.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Shocking stat of the day: US fixed-income ETF trading volume as a % of total ETF volume is up to 27...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Shocking stat of the day:
US fixed-income ETF trading volume as a % of total ETF volume is up to 27%, its highest in at least 6 years.
This figure has more than doubled over the last several weeks.
By comparison, in June, fixed-income ETFs accounted for just 7% of total ETF volume.
Since 2021, there have been only a couple of brief periods where this figure exceeded 20%.
This comes as the surge in Treasury yields accelerated, with the 10Y Note yield surpassing 5.30% and the 30Y Note yield surpassing 5.60%, both for the first time since 2002.
Investors are capitalizing on the historic moves in the bond market.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Ever watched a "sure thing" take -50% out of a position? Now it needs +100% just to get back to eve...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
Ever watched a "sure thing" take -50% out of a position?
Now it needs +100% just to get back to even. At -80%, it needs +400%.
That's why the MAX exists.
Set your sizing range by asset class BEFORE the trade. Equities 2-6% Fixed Income 3-10% Foreign Currency 4-12% Commodities 1-4%
Single stocks run 2-6% on the long side and 1-3% on the short side. Every max is per position, not per asset class.
Then scale inside those boundaries in 50-150bps increments. Never a full position in one move. The -6% stop is a backstop, and it only applies once a position is already at its max.
Consistency matters.
The full sizing framework lives in Hedgeye Education https://app.hedgeye.com/education

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US high-yield credit market stress is rising: Credit spreads for CCC-rated and lower corporate...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US high-yield credit market stress is rising:
Credit spreads for CCC-rated and lower corporate bonds are up to 12.0%, their widest level since November 2022.
Over the last 5 months, this figure has surged +298 basis points, surpassing the April 2025 peak of 11.4%.
This represents a comparable increase to that seen during the 2022 bear market and the February-April 2025 market correction.
If this pace continues, credit spreads for the lowest-rated US corporate bonds will exceed the 2022 peak of 12.9% as soon as this month.
To put this into perspective, the 2020 pandemic high was 19.6%.
Credit stress is rising sharply beneath the surface.

If this pace continues, credit spreads for the lowest-rated US corporate bonds will exceed the 2022 peak of 12.9% as soon as this month.

To put this into perspective, the 2020 pandemic high was 19.6%.

Credit stress is rising sharply beneath the surface.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$UBER TO ACQUIRE EZCATER FOR $2.3B IN CASH, EXPANDING UBER EATS INTO CATERING
Uber is buying ezCater, a U.S. workplace meals and catering platform with 140,000+ restaurant partners and more than $2.5B in trailing 12-month gross bookings.
ezCater is growing at a high-teens rate YoY, has average orders above $400, and is profitable on a non-GAAP operating income basis. Uber expects the deal to be margin accretive.
After closing, ezCater will be integrated with Uber Eats and Uber for Business, giving Uber a larger presence in high-value group and enterprise food orders.
item.content:encoded:
$UBER TO ACQUIRE EZCATER FOR $2.3B IN CASH, EXPANDING UBER EATS INTO CATERING

Uber is buying ezCater, a U.S. workplace meals and catering platform with 140,000+ restaurant partners and more than $2.5B in trailing 12-month gross bookings.

ezCater is growing at a high-teens rate YoY, has average orders above $400, and is profitable on a non-GAAP operating income basis. Uber expects the deal to be margin accretive.

After closing, ezCater will be integrated with Uber Eats and Uber for Business, giving Uber a larger presence in high-value group and enterprise food orders.

item.title: @wallstengine: $AMD CEO Lisa Su says demand is still running above supply and expects strong demand for compute to...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AMD CEO Lisa Su says demand is still running above supply and expects strong demand for compute to continue for the next several years, with AMD planning to “substantially increase” supply in 2027.
Su said AMD has already increased supply this year but “could definitely use more,” thanked TSMC for bringing additional capacity online, and noted that memory remains broadly supply constrained.
AMD is working with memory suppliers and customers to make sure capacity comes online together, while keeping its current business model unchanged.
Su also called Taiwan “very critical” to AMD and said the company plans to increase its investment there, while continuing to look at new packaging technologies.
Source: Reuters

item.title: @wallstengine: DEEPSEEK SET TO RAISE AT LEAST $12B IN TENCENT, CATL-LED ROUND AHEAD OF 2027 IPO DeepSeek is nearin...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
DEEPSEEK SET TO RAISE AT LEAST $12B IN TENCENT, CATL-LED ROUND AHEAD OF 2027 IPO
DeepSeek is nearing at least $12 billion in new funding, significantly above its initial target of roughly $7.5 billion, as investor demand surged following the release of its latest AI model, according to Bloomberg.
Tencent and battery giant CATL are among the largest investors in the round. Based on signed term sheets, the final raise could approach 100 billion yuan, or roughly $15 billion.
DeepSeek had originally targeted a valuation of about 500 billion yuan, roughly $75 billion, for the financing.
Once the round closes, the company is expected to begin restructuring in preparation for an IPO targeted for early 2027. Reuters previously reported DeepSeek was preparing for a potential mainland China listing.
The new capital will help fund DeepSeek’s rapidly growing AI infrastructure needs. The company plans to deploy at least 160,000 of Huawei’s highest-end AI accelerators at a massive new data center in Inner Mongolia, while continuing to develop open AI models and pursue artificial general intelligence.
DeepSeek previously raised more than $7 billion in its first external funding round earlier this year, with Tencent and CATL also participating.
The latest financing would position DeepSeek for one of the most closely watched Chinese technology IPOs in years, alongside rival Moonshot AI, which is also targeting a 2027 public listing.
Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @wallstengine: MOONSHOT AI EYES EARLY 2027 HONG KONG IPO AFTER VALUATION HITS $50B Chinese AI startup Moonshot AI...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
MOONSHOT AI EYES EARLY 2027 HONG KONG IPO AFTER VALUATION HITS $50B
Chinese AI startup Moonshot AI has completed its final private funding round at a valuation of about $50B and is preparing for a potential Hong Kong IPO in Q1 2027.
The company is considering raising as much as $5B and could begin early investor meetings as soon as this month.
Moonshot’s ARR is currently around $1B and is expected to reach $2B by December, up from roughly $300M in June.
The company, known for its Kimi AI models, was valued at $31.5B in a previous funding round this summer.
Bank of America is serving as overall coordinator for the IPO alongside CICC, Deutsche Bank and Goldman Sachs. Moonshot has reportedly already filed confidentially for the listing.
Alibaba, Tencent and 5Y Capital are among its existing backers.
The IPO timing could still change, with Moonshot also reportedly facing a Chinese regulatory data-security probe alongside DeepSeek.
Source: Bloomberg

Chinese AI startup Moonshot AI has completed its final private funding round at a valuation of about $50B and is preparing for a potential Hong Kong IPO in Q1 2027.

The company is considering raising as much as $5B and could begin early investor meetings as soon as this month.

Moonshot’s ARR is currently around $1B and is expected to reach $2B by December, up from roughly $300M in June.

The company, known for its Kimi AI models, was valued at $31.5B in a previous funding round this summer.

Bank of America is serving as overall coordinator for the IPO alongside CICC, Deutsche Bank and Goldman Sachs. Moonshot has reportedly already filed confidentially for the listing.

Alibaba, Tencent and 5Y Capital are among its existing backers.

The IPO timing could still change, with Moonshot also reportedly facing a Chinese regulatory data-security probe alongside DeepSeek.

Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US economy has now experienced 78 consecutive months of expansion, the 6th-longest bu...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US economy has now experienced 78 consecutive months of expansion, the 6th-longest business cycle since 1854.
This is well above the long-term average of ~49 months and the median of ~38 months.
By comparison, the longest period without a recession was between 2009 and 2020, at 128 months.
All 5 of the most recent US expansions rank among the 7 longest economic growth periods since business cycle dating began in 1854.
Unconventional monetary policy, historically large budget deficits, alongside the AI investment boom, appear to be extending the duration of business cycles.
The data says the US economy is remarkably strong.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: American wages are not keeping up with inflation. US average hourly earnings adjusted for inflation...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
American wages are not keeping up with inflation.
US average hourly earnings adjusted for inflation fell -0.3% YoY in September, marking the 5th consecutive decline in real wages.
This follows a -0.2% YoY decrease in August, -0.3% in July, and -0.8% in June, the largest decline since May 2023.
This marks a sharp deterioration from +1.3% YoY growth in real wages recorded in February.
This all comes as US CPI inflation has remained above +3.0% for 6 consecutive months, the longest such streak since mid-2024.
Meanwhile, in nominal terms, average hourly earnings rose +3.0% YoY in September, their slowest growth since May 2021.
Nominal wage growth has been in a downtrend since March 2025, when earnings grew +4.2% YoY.
Inflation is eroding the spending power of Americans.

item.title: @wallstengine: Nokia $NOK CEO Hotard says AI infra demand remains strong and supply constraints are the main thing...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nokia $NOK CEO Hotard says AI infra demand remains strong and supply constraints are the main thing slowing the buildout
“I don’t think you can say in any manner we’re overbuilding today”
“If we could build 2x faster, our customers could build 2x faster, they probably would”
Hotard said that gives him confidence “we’re still in the early days” of the AI buildout.
He also argued demand does not depend on constant releases of new frontier models:
“Even if we didn’t have another frontier model released in the next three years, we could probably make tremendous progress just deploying the technology that’s there today.”
Memory shortages and power availability remain among the biggest constraints.
Source: CNBC / ht @ArjunKharpal

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US business spending on computers and peripheral equipment, a key GDP measure of AI CapEx...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US business spending on computers and peripheral equipment, a key GDP measure of AI CapEx, jumped +$20.5 billion in Q2 2026 to a record $420.1 billion.
This includes spending on physical computing hardware, including servers, data storage, personal computers, and peripherals, making it a useful proxy for AI-related hardware investment.
This marks the 6th consecutive quarterly increase, totaling +$233.6 billion, or +125%.
Since Q3 2023, spending on computers and peripheral equipment has nearly tripled.
Furthermore, this metric does not fully capture AI CapEx, including AI data centers, communication equipment, and software.
The AI investment boom is reaching unprecedented levels.

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI IN TALKS WITH UAE FUNDS, BLACKROCK FOR $30B FUNDING ROUND AT ~$1.4T VALUATION: BBG
OpenAI is in talks with several UAE investment funds, including Abu Dhabi-based MGX, to help anchor a new financing round of at least $30B.
UAE investors have discussed contributing as much as $10B collectively, while BlackRock $BLK is also in discussions to participate alongside the syndicate.
Existing backers Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz have discussed investing, while OpenAI has also held talks with the University of California’s endowment.
The company is presenting investors with a fixed ~$1.4T pre-money valuation rather than negotiating the valuation through a traditional lead-investor process.
The fundraising comes as OpenAI pushes potential IPO plans until at least 2027 while continuing to raise large amounts of capital to fund AI development and infrastructure.
MGX has previously invested in both OpenAI and Anthropic and earlier this year raised nearly $50B to invest across AI infrastructure and technology.
Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @wallstengine: Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley have begun syndicating a $60B debt package tied to Anthrop...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley have begun syndicating a $60B debt package tied to Anthropic’s lease of Google-designed AI chips supplied through Broadcom $AVGO, the largest chip-financing deal to date.
The financing includes:
• $42B of senior secured debt supported by Broadcom, which has begun bank syndication • $18B of junior debt without Broadcom guarantees • Blackstone has already committed about $9B to the junior tranche
The proceeds are expected to fund Anthropic’s 2027 chip orders, with lease payments beginning once the chips are delivered.
Broadcom is partially backstopping the financing to help lower Anthropic’s borrowing costs. Its A- credit rating could also allow the $42B senior portion to eventually be sold to a broader investor base through private placements or investment-grade bonds.
The deal centers on Google $GOOGL tensor processing units being developed with Broadcom as an alternative to Nvidia $NVDA GPUs for large-scale AI workloads.
Anthropic could also issue up to $42B of convertible notes to Broadcom to cover lease payments, according to Broadcom filings cited by FT.
Source: FT
item.content:encoded:
Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley have begun syndicating a $60B debt package tied to Anthropic’s lease of Google-designed AI chips supplied through Broadcom $AVGO, the largest chip-financing deal to date.

• $18B of junior debt without Broadcom guarantees
• Blackstone has already committed about $9B to the junior tranche

The proceeds are expected to fund Anthropic’s 2027 chip orders, with lease payments beginning once the chips are delivered.

Broadcom is partially backstopping the financing to help lower Anthropic’s borrowing costs. Its A- credit rating could also allow the $42B senior portion to eventually be sold to a broader investor base through private placements or investment-grade bonds.

The deal centers on Google $GOOGL tensor processing units being developed with Broadcom as an alternative to Nvidia $NVDA GPUs for large-scale AI workloads.

Anthropic could also issue up to $42B of convertible notes to Broadcom to cover lease payments, according to Broadcom filings cited by FT.

Source: FT

item.title: @wallstengine: Nvidia-backed Reflection AI has launched Beam, a 501B-parameter open-weight AI model built for codi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nvidia-backed Reflection AI has launched Beam, a 501B-parameter open-weight AI model built for coding, reasoning and AI-agent workloads.
Beam is aimed at competing with leading open-weight models from China. Beam is a text-only mixture-of-experts model with:
• 501B total parameters, 23B active • 1M-token context window • Pretrained on 23.8T tokens • Built for coding, reasoning, tool use and agentic workloads
Reflection says Beam performs comparably with Z .ai’s GLM-5.2 on advanced reasoning benchmarks while using 3-4x less inference compute. The company’s benchmark claims have not yet been independently verified.
Beam’s reinforcement-learning run used 10,500 NVIDIA $NVDA GB300 GPUs for four weeks and generated more than 100M rollouts. Its base model was pretrained on 6,144 GB300 GPUs in under four weeks.
Reflection is targeting enterprises, developers and sovereign governments, with a broader strategy around customized “AI factories” that can connect organizations’ proprietary data to locally controlled AI systems.
The NVIDIA-backed startup has also signed more than $7B worth of compute deals with SpaceX and Nebius $NBIS to secure access to GB300 infrastructure through 2029.
Reflection plans to release Beam’s weights under an Apache 2.0 license later this month, along with its technical report, model card and tools for running, evaluating and fine-tuning the model.

Nvidia-backed Reflection AI has launched Beam, a 501B-parameter open-weight AI model built for coding, reasoning and AI-agent workloads.

Beam is aimed at competing with leading open-weight models from China. Beam is a text-only mixture-of-experts model with:

• 501B total parameters, 23B active
• 1M-token context window
• Pretrained on 23.8T tokens
• Built for coding, reasoning, tool use and agentic workloads

Reflection says Beam performs comparably with Z .ai’s GLM-5.2 on advanced reasoning benchmarks while using 3-4x less inference compute. The company’s benchmark claims have not yet been independently verified.

Beam’s reinforcement-learning run used 10,500 NVIDIA $NVDA GB300 GPUs for four weeks and generated more than 100M rollouts. Its base model was pretrained on 6,144 GB300 GPUs in under four weeks.

Reflection is targeting enterprises, developers and sovereign governments, with a broader strategy around customized “AI factories” that can connect organizations’ proprietary data to locally controlled AI systems.

The NVIDIA-backed startup has also signed more than $7B worth of compute deals with SpaceX and Nebius $NBIS to secure access to GB300 infrastructure through 2029.

Reflection plans to release Beam’s weights under an Apache 2.0 license later this month, along with its technical report, model card and tools for running, evaluating and fine-tuning the model.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: History points to further weakness in market breadth: Since 1990, October has experienced the weake...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
History points to further weakness in market breadth:
Since 1990, October has experienced the weakest market breadth of any month, with just 51.7% of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day moving average.
This follows September, when an average of 53.1% of S&P 500 stocks traded above their 50-day moving average over the same period.
By comparison, December has had stronger breadth, with 64.2% of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day moving average.
Subsequently, January has seen the 2nd-strongest breadth, at 62.2%.
Currently, just 21.4% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day moving average, down from ~70% in mid-August, marking their lowest reading since early April.
Furthermore, on Friday, new 52-week lows on the S&P 500 outnumbered new highs for the 14th consecutive trading day.
Market breadth is extremely weak.

item.title: @wallstengine: UTAH BECOMES FIRST STATE TO LET AI ISSUE PRESCRIPTIONS Nolla Health is launching a Utah pilot where...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
UTAH BECOMES FIRST STATE TO LET AI ISSUE PRESCRIPTIONS
Nolla Health is launching a Utah pilot where its AI can assess acne, review a patient’s medical history and send prescriptions directly to pharmacies without a doctor approving every prescription.
The program is limited to eight approved topical acne treatments, with no pills or hormone therapies.
Doctor oversight will be phased: › First 100 patients: doctor approval before prescriptions are sent
› Next 400: AI sends prescriptions directly, with doctors reviewing them afterward each week
› After that: doctors review at least 10% of prescriptions each month
Utah granted Nolla a narrow exemption from the usual requirement that a licensed human prescriber write the prescription.
Nolla costs about $5/month, with compounded medications around $50/month, versus roughly $150-$300 for a typical dermatology visit.
https://x.com/luiswenus/status/2107123349348298800/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US consumer confidence is collapsing. The Consumer Confidence Index dropped -6.7 points in Septembe...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US consumer confidence is collapsing.
The Consumer Confidence Index dropped -6.7 points in September, to 81.9, its lowest since April 2014.
This marks its 4th consecutive monthly decline, totaling -11.2 points.
The Present Situation Index fell -7.9 points, to 109.3, its lowest since February 2021.
At the same time, the Expectations Index fell -5.9 points, to 63.6, its lowest since April 2025, marking its 3rd consecutive monthly decline.
Over the last 6 months, confidence across all age groups and nearly all income groups has declined.
Consumers are also increasingly citing high prices, the cost of goods and services, and oil and gasoline prices as major factors weighing on the economy.
US consumer confidence is at crisis levels.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US stock market is in its own league. US stock market cap now accounts for 45% of the world equ...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US stock market is in its own league.
US stock market cap now accounts for 45% of the world equity market value, the most among any other major country or region.
This is nearly triple the combined proportion of China and Hong Kong, at 16%.
Europe and the rest of Asia-Pacific follow, accounting for 13% and 11% of global market cap, respectively.
By comparison, Japan, the world's 3rd-largest stock market, represents just 6%.
Meanwhile, the Middle East and Africa account for 5%, while Canada and Latin America make up 3% and 1%, respectively.
The scale of the US equity market relative to the rest of the world is unprecedented.

The scale of the US equity market relative to the rest of the world is unprecedented.

US job cut announcements dropped -20% YoY in September, to 43,281, the lowest September total since 2022.
In Q3, planned layoffs fell -36% YoY, to 129,591, the lowest quarterly figure since Q4 2023.
This brings year-to-date announcements down -39% YoY, to 573,195, the lowest since 2022.
This is also the 7th month of 2026 with job cuts below the corresponding month of the prior year.
The tech sector saw the most announcements last month and year-to-date, at 10,799 and 165,925 respectively.
Meanwhile, market and economic conditions accounted for 8,789 announced job cuts in September, or 20% of all layoffs, bringing the year-to-date total to 114,124, the 2nd-highest of any cited reason after AI.
US employers are taking a wait-and-see approach to layoffs.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz have sharply rebounded: Persian Gulf crude oil exports surpassed...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Oil flows in the Strait of Hormuz have sharply rebounded:
Persian Gulf crude oil exports surpassed 14 million barrels per day last week for the first time since the Iran War began on February 28th.
This marks an over +210% increase from the ~4.5 million barrels per day low seen in March.
As a result, the 4-week average is up to 14 million barrels per day, the highest level in 6 months.
Persian Gulf crude oil exports have now recovered to ~80% of their pre-war levels.
This comes as the US military has increasingly secured the Strait of Hormuz and established a two-way shipping corridor along the coast of Oman, allowing oil convoys to resume through the waterway.
Meanwhile, refined fuel shipments, including gasoline, diesel and jet fuel, remain at only around 50% of pre-war levels, as these products are more expensive to transport than crude oil and some refineries in the Persian Gulf that were damaged during the early stages of the war have also yet to fully resume operations.
Oil flows are coming back, but the fuel market is still under intense pressure.

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI-related employment is surging:
AI-linked roles have accounted for more than +750,000 new jobs created in the US since 2023, according to LinkedIn estimates.
This surge has been led by data annotators, with +282,000 new positions created, followed by data center jobs at +117,000, and AI engineers at +105,000.
As a result, these 3 categories have accounted for +504,000 new jobs.
AI-related positions also offer significantly higher pay, with a median salary of ~$180,000 on LinkedIn, compared to $80,000 across all jobs.
This comes as the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure, particularly the buildout of data centers, is driving stronger demand for labor.
The AI boom is reshaping the US job market.

item.description: @KeithMcCullough Generally: an unhedged spot ETP has ~1.0 beta to its underlying, with the underlying's vol. A hedged ETF uses an options overlay to change effective exposure, so beta and realized vol become variable. Measurement of a hedged ETFs effectiveness lies in risk adjusted returns (think Sharpe or Sortino ratio).
