item.title: @WOLF_Financial: Here’s what Nebius $NBIS owns, what it has acquired and where it has invested over the years. Acqui...
item.dc:creator: @WOLF_Financial
item.description:
Here’s what Nebius $NBIS owns, what it has acquired and where it has invested over the years.
Acquisitions and technology deals
Eigen AI: AI inference optimization. The 2026 cash-and-stock acquisition was valued at roughly $643M when announced.
Tavily: Web search for AI agents. Acquired in February 2026, with $177.3M paid in cash at closing, plus equity awards and potential additional payments.
Inferize: Technology that loads AI models faster and reduces idle GPU time. Acquired Oct. 1, 2026. Financial terms were not disclosed.
Clarifai: Added its core engineering and research team, patents and licensed inference technology in May 2026. Not an acquisition of the entire company; terms were undisclosed.
Operating businesses
Nebius AI Cloud: Its core platform for AI training, inference and deployment.
Avride: Autonomous vehicles and delivery robots. Uber and Nebius announced up to $375M in combined investment and commercial commitments in 2025, not Nebius funding alone.
TripleTen: Technology education, career retraining and skills development.
Equity investments
ClickHouse: Minority stake in the real-time database and analytics company. Nebius invested an additional $50M in its May 2025 financing.
Toloka: Equity stake in the AI training-data and evaluation company. Nebius invested $39M in its 2025 financing transaction and retained a noncontrolling interest.

item.title: @hassaanraza: Yesterday we previewed Griffin, a Human Interaction Model capable of seeing, hearing, sounding, and...
item.dc:creator: @hassaanraza
item.description:
Yesterday we previewed Griffin, a Human Interaction Model capable of seeing, hearing, sounding, and looking like a human does. There have been a lot of questions, so I wanted to take a moment to share our thoughts.
By way of introduction: Tavus is a research lab focused on enabling machines to meet us where we are, and to understand the nuances of how we communicate beyond words.
Griffin, our latest model, isn’t publicly available yet. Yesterday’s announcement was a limited research preview to demonstrate what the model is capable of. With AI progressing so quickly, we prefer to share breakthroughs openly and in real-time as we work on a safe public release.
Face-to-face is how we evolutionarily communicate, it carries the most meaning and intent, and we want computers to be able to help with work that benefits from that emotional understanding, expression, and immersion. Some examples of the kinds of use cases we care deeply about:
- A tutor that can build understanding of how a student learns, see exactly when there is confusion or disengagement, and adapt the lesson to fit them.
- A health expert that can answer any questions about your upcoming appointment or prescription, at the pace you want, at any time you need, even on a weekend.
- A language coach that you can practice speaking with, that can correct your movement and pronunciation, and help build confidence to have real conversations
- Or the perfect assistant for everyone, that understands intent, knows how you work and remembers what matters.
We’re working with partners on safeguards and systems for disclosure, as well as inviting discussions with officials around wider regulation and safe use. People will always know they’re interacting with AI, while providing an interface that removes the need to ‘speak computer’.
We believe in a future where computers understand us well enough to make technology more accessible, more useful, and make us more capable as humans. That is the world we want to build, and we understand the responsibility to do so safely.

By way of introduction: Tavus is a research lab focused on enabling machines to meet us where we are, and to understand the nuances of how we communicate beyond words.

Griffin, our latest model, isn’t publicly available yet. Yesterday’s announcement was a limited research preview to demonstrate what the model is capable of. With AI progressing so quickly, we prefer to share breakthroughs openly and in real-time as we work on a safe public release.

Face-to-face is how we evolutionarily communicate, it carries the most meaning and intent, and we want computers to be able to help with work that benefits from that emotional understanding, expression, and immersion. Some examples of the kinds of use cases we care deeply about:

- A tutor that can build understanding of how a student learns, see exactly when there is confusion or disengagement, and adapt the lesson to fit them.

- A health expert that can answer any questions about your upcoming appointment or prescription, at the pace you want, at any time you need, even on a weekend.

- A language coach that you can practice speaking with, that can correct your movement and pronunciation, and help build confidence to have real conversations

- Or the perfect assistant for everyone, that understands intent, knows how you work and remembers what matters.

We’re working with partners on safeguards and systems for disclosure, as well as inviting discussions with officials around wider regulation and safe use. People will always know they’re interacting with AI, while providing an interface that removes the need to ‘speak computer’.

We believe in a future where computers understand us well enough to make technology more accessible, more useful, and make us more capable as humans. That is the world we want to build, and we understand the responsibility to do so safely.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Inflationary pressures are intensifying in the US manufacturing sector: The ISM Manufacturing Price...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Inflationary pressures are intensifying in the US manufacturing sector:
The ISM Manufacturing Prices Paid Index surged +6.8 points in September, to 77.9, its highest since May.
This also marks its largest monthly increase since February.
Year-to-date, the index has soared +19.4 points, its third-biggest 9-month increase since 2021.
Meanwhile, the ISM Manufacturing PMI index eased slightly in September by -0.1 point, to 54.5, remaining in expansion for the 9th consecutive month, its longest streak since 2022.
Furthermore, new orders rose +1.6 points, to 55.3, also posting their 9th consecutive monthly expansion.
And, the backlog of unfilled orders jumped +4.6 points, to 56.4, its 2nd-highest level since May 2022.
Manufacturing price pressures are building as elevated demand puts further strain on capacity.

Furthermore, new orders rose +1.6 points, to 55.3, also posting their 9th consecutive monthly expansion.

item.title: @wallstengine: $META is opening Muse up to custom hardware. Nat Friedman announced Muse Gadgets, with open-source...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META is opening Muse up to custom hardware.
Nat Friedman announced Muse Gadgets, with open-source ESP32 firmware and a Linux SDK that let developers connect Muse to displays, speakers, sensors, actuators, Raspberry Pis and other devices. Every gadget pairs with Muse using an SDK token.
Meta also built Muse Home Link, a small USB-C device that connects Muse to your home network so it can interact with compatible TVs, speakers, printers and anything exposing a local HTTP API.
Meta manufactured 5,000 Home Links. They’re expected to ship in October and are free to active U.S. Muse subscribers, one per subscriber, while supplies last.

item.title: @eglyman: we put on a broadway musical about accounts payable. slate called it "a glorified ad for a tech com...
item.dc:creator: @eglyman
item.description:
we put on a broadway musical about accounts payable.
slate called it "a glorified ad for a tech company." correct. it was also the most fun we've ever had as a company.
the part i didn't expect was what happened after. a flood of messages from theater folks in new york saying it meant the world to them. billy porter told the crowd that industrials like this paid his rent for decades, until they disappeared in the early 2000s.
for most of the last century, when a company had something to say, it hired composers, choreographers and actors. somewhere along the way we decided marketing should be cheap, measurable and forgettable.
i hope more companies lose their minds a little. make something people feel.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Shocking stat of the day: Each of the top 4 S&P 500 companies is now larger than the entire Russell...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Shocking stat of the day:
Each of the top 4 S&P 500 companies is now larger than the entire Russell 2000 Index, which has a total market cap of $3.5 trillion.
Nvidia, $NVDA, alone, with a $5.7 trillion market cap, exceeds the small-cap index by $2.2 trillion.
At the same time, Apple, $AAPL, with its $4.9 trillion market cap, is worth $1.4 trillion more than the Russell 2000.
Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, are valued at $4.2 trillion and $3.8 trillion, respectively, also surpassing the combined market cap of the Russell.
These 4 big tech stocks are now collectively valued at a massive $18.6 trillion, accounting for 26% of the S&P 500’s total market cap.
Meanwhile, the Russell 2000 represents ~7% of the total US equity market, despite containing nearly 2,000 companies.
Big tech has never been bigger.

Alphabet, $GOOGL, and Microsoft, $MSFT, are valued at $4.2 trillion and $3.8 trillion, respectively, also surpassing the combined market cap of the Russell.

item.title: @wallstengine: Disney $DIS is expanding its content licensing deal with Netflix $NFLX, sending both library titles...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Disney $DIS is expanding its content licensing deal with Netflix $NFLX, sending both library titles and current-season shows to the platform on a nonexclusive basis.
Titles include:
• All five Ice Age films • Percy Jackson S1-2 • Will Trent S1-4 • Shifting Gears S1-2 • Tracker S1-3 internationally • Soul, Elio and Raya and the Last Dragon • Felicity, Revenge and Army Wives
Disney is also using some of the Netflix windows as promotion ahead of new Disney+ seasons and theatrical releases.
The titles currently on Disney+ and Hulu will remain there.
item.content:encoded:

item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
NVIDIA $NVDA is launching a new 64GB DGX Spark on Oct. 23, starting at $4,999 through Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI.
It keeps the GB10 Grace Blackwell chip and supports models up to 100B parameters locally.
Two units can be linked over 200GbE to pool 128GB of memory and run models up to 200B parameters, with NVIDIA reporting up to 1.7x performance vs. one system.
NVIDIA Sync will automatically configure the two-system cluster.

item.title: @wallstengine: B. Riley Downgrades $ASTS to Neutral from Buy, Cuts PT to $65 from $85 Crawford says the risk/rewar...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
B. Riley Downgrades $ASTS to Neutral from Buy, Cuts PT to $65 from $85
Crawford says the risk/reward has “swung back toward balance,” citing “arguably stronger competitive alternatives, delayed launch, and rising constellation costs, potentially including additional spectrum.”
BlueBird 11’s full deployment was confirmed about 35 days after ASTS announced successful deployment of BlueBirds 12 and 13, despite all three launching on August 5.
His concern is “what prices consumers ultimately will bear for added space-based connectivity” as lower-cost competitors emerge.
Viasat and Space42’s Equatys venture could begin launching a constellation that may reach 2,800 satellites as soon as 2028.
He sees a potential Rocket Lab partnership with Equatys as a greater threat than Rocket Lab competing independently.
Crawford still views D2D as a “multiple-winner market” and ASTS among its leaders. But with subscriber uptake and service pricing data still to come, he believes “shares fairly reflect what we know today.”
Analyst: Mike Crawford
item.content:encoded:
B. Riley Downgrades $ASTS to Neutral from Buy, Cuts PT to $65 from $85

Crawford says the risk/reward has “swung back toward balance,” citing “arguably stronger competitive alternatives, delayed launch, and rising constellation costs, potentially including additional spectrum.”

BlueBird 11’s full deployment was confirmed about 35 days after ASTS announced successful deployment of BlueBirds 12 and 13, despite all three launching on August 5.

His concern is “what prices consumers ultimately will bear for added space-based connectivity” as lower-cost competitors emerge.

Viasat and Space42’s Equatys venture could begin launching a constellation that may reach 2,800 satellites as soon as 2028.

He sees a potential Rocket Lab partnership with Equatys as a greater threat than Rocket Lab competing independently.

Crawford still views D2D as a “multiple-winner market” and ASTS among its leaders. But with subscriber uptake and service pricing data still to come, he believes “shares fairly reflect what we know today.”

Analyst: Mike Crawford

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US personal savings rate fell -0.5 percentage points in August, to 4.1%, the lowest l...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US personal savings rate fell -0.5 percentage points in August, to 4.1%, the lowest level since November 2021.
Since January 2025, this figure has declined -1.6 percentage points.
Excluding the 2022 drop, when elevated inflation eroded purchasing power and forced American households to spend more on essentials, the savings rate is now at its lowest level since 2008.
Meanwhile, the 5-year average of this metric fell to 5.4%, the lowest in 14 years.
By comparison, before the 2020 pandemic, the average savings rate was ~6.0%.
Households are depleting their savings amid ongoing inflation.

item.title: @wallstengine: Volantis Semiconductor raised an $88M Series A, bringing total funding to $97M, to attack AI’s memo...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Volantis Semiconductor raised an $88M Series A, bringing total funding to $97M, to attack AI’s memory bottleneck with photonics.
Backers include: OpenAI's Sam Altman SemiAnalysis'S Dylan Patel Jeff Dean John Doerr and others
The company is building an optical “fabric” designed to connect AI processors to much larger pools of memory while dramatically increasing bandwidth.
Volantis says its architecture can boost both memory capacity and bandwidth by more than 10x, targeting inference for models larger than 10 trillion parameters at speeds of up to 10,000 tokens per second per user.
The core problem it is trying to solve is the “memory wall.” Volantis argues today’s architectures force a tradeoff: on-chip SRAM offers very high bandwidth but limited capacity, while HBM-based GPUs and TPUs offer far more memory but eventually run into bandwidth constraints as models scale.
Its approach replaces more of the electrical data movement with optics, using custom integrated micro-VCSEL lasers and eliminating traditional optical fiber to push much more data across short distances inside AI systems.
The company says it has already transmitted data more than 10x farther than similarly tiny electrical wires inside a chip package, and its next-generation design has already taped out.
The near-term use case is much faster inference.
Volantis says a coding agent that currently takes around 30 minutes could potentially complete the same task in roughly 30 seconds, while also lowering cost per token through higher throughput and cheaper pooled memory.
If the technology scales as planned, the bigger idea is enabling much larger context windows, entire code repositories in context, and AI systems that are currently limited more by memory movement than raw compute.

item.title: @wallstengine: $GOOGL JUST PUT ITS AI CHIPS INTO ORBIT FOR THE FIRST TIME Google and Planet Labs $PL have successf...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$GOOGL JUST PUT ITS AI CHIPS INTO ORBIT FOR THE FIRST TIME
Google and Planet Labs $PL have successfully launched Project Suncatcher M1 aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission.
Planet says it has already made contact with the spacecraft and begun commissioning. This is the first-ever in-orbit test of Google’s Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs.
The refrigerator-sized prototype carries four Trillium TPUs, Google’s custom AI accelerators.
This is not yet an orbital data center. The goal is to see whether the same type of AI hardware Google uses on Earth can survive launch and reliably run machine-learning workloads in low Earth orbit.
There are three major engineering problems Google is testing:
RADIATION: cosmic radiation can corrupt calculations or damage electronics. Google previously tested Trillium TPUs with proton radiation and found they could withstand more total radiation than expected over a five-year mission.
COOLING: there is no air in space, so fans cannot cool the chips. Heat has to be moved through heat pipes into radiators and then emitted away from the spacecraft. The current prototype is expected to run AI workloads in roughly 15-minute bursts before allowing the system to cool.
NETWORKING: Google’s long-term plan is not one satellite, but clusters of satellites carrying dozens of TPUs each and connected through high-speed laser links.
Google estimates future AI workloads could require tens of terabits per second between satellites. Its ground prototype has already demonstrated 800 Gbps in each direction.
Why put AI compute in space at all?
In the right low-Earth orbit, solar panels can generate up to 8x more power than on Earth because satellites can receive near-continuous sunlight, reducing one of the biggest constraints facing AI data centers: electricity.
The economics:
Google estimates that if launch costs eventually fall below roughly $200 per kilogram by the mid-2030s, the cost of operating compute in space could begin approaching the energy cost of comparable terrestrial data centers.

item.description:
BOEING WORKERS APPROVE NEW 4-YEAR CONTRACT, AVOIDING POTENTIAL STRIKE
Boeing $BA’s largest white-collar union approved a new contract covering about 17,000 engineers, scientists, designers and technicians.
The deal includes a 10% guaranteed wage increase at ratification, followed by 4% annual raises and up to an additional 2% based on performance.
The vote removes the risk of a strike as early as Oct. 7 that could have disrupted 737 MAX 10 and 777X certification work, production ramp plans and aircraft deliveries.
68% of the professional unit and 53%+ of the technical unit voted in favor.

AI is all that matters for markets right now.
AI infrastructure companies now account for 40% of the S&P 500’s market capitalization.
At the same time, just 3 chipmaker firms represent 28% of the MSCI Emerging Markets Index.
AI-related companies also account for 49% of investment-grade bond issuance so far in 2026.
The concentration is even more extreme in private markets, with AI capturing 87% of venture capital funding year-to-date.

AI has become the market.

item.title: @wallstengine: IF YOU’RE A FINANCIAL ANALYST, THIS IS WORTH PAYING ATTENTION TO These guys just launched Filot Aut...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
IF YOU’RE A FINANCIAL ANALYST, THIS IS WORTH PAYING ATTENTION TO
These guys just launched Filot Autopilot, a finance tool that can basically keep your financial models updated for you as companies report earnings.
So your laptop could be closed, earnings could drop, and the system can still pull the new filings, transcripts and numbers, update the model in the background, and have it ready for you to review.
And I think that’s really the interesting part here.
A lot of an analyst’s time during earnings season is still spent doing pretty repetitive work, updating numbers, checking models, making sure everything ties out.
If tools like this can handle more of that reliably, it probably means analysts can spend more time on the higher-value part of the job: actually understanding what changed, what matters, and what the market might be missing.
https://x.com/bjornbirkelund/status/2105696744633733342/video/1

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Investors have rarely been this bullish on tech. Long speculative positioning in Nasdaq futures is...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Investors have rarely been this bullish on tech.
Long speculative positioning in Nasdaq futures is up to nearly 50% of open interest, its highest since 2017.
This covers hedge funds, CTAs, and other institutional investors trading Nasdaq futures.
In other words, the net long Nasdaq futures position of these investors equals ~50% of all currently open Nasdaq futures contracts.
This marks a sharp reversal from a net short position as a % of open interest just a few weeks ago.
By comparison, Nasdaq net long positioning was below 25% of open interest for most of 2021-2025.
Meanwhile, net short positioning in Russell 2000 futures is down to -30% of open interest, its most bearish level since late 2025.
Investors are becoming extremely bullish on tech.

item.title: @wallstengine: A NEW LAW FIRM JUST RAISED $17M TO REBUILD HOW COMPANIES HANDLE LEGAL WORK Arceus just launched wit...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
A NEW LAW FIRM JUST RAISED $17M TO REBUILD HOW COMPANIES HANDLE LEGAL WORK
Arceus just launched with $17M in funding led by Greycroft, with participation from Craft Ventures, South Park Commons and others.
Arceus is a law firm that uses AI and software to handle commercial legal work faster.
Companies can send over contracts like NDAs, MSAs, DPAs and vendor agreements, and Arceus handles the review, drafting, redlining and negotiation.
AI is used to gather context, speed up the workflow and help with the repetitive parts, but licensed attorneys are still responsible for reviewing, drafting, redlining and negotiating the contracts.
Arceus says its average contract review takes around 4–6 hours
It also uses flat-fee pricing instead of billable hours, so companies know what the work will cost before it starts.
And instead of constantly emailing outside counsel, clients can submit requests directly through Slack and get updates there.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The US corporate high-yield bond market is under serious pressure. The effective yield on US high-y...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The US corporate high-yield bond market is under serious pressure.
The effective yield on US high-yield corporate bonds is up to 8.03%, its highest since April 2025.
This figure has surged +104 basis points over the last 5 weeks, marking its largest 5-week increase in 17 months.
As a result, high-yield corporate bond spreads are up to 3.02%, their highest since early-April.
This represents the extra yield investors demand, on average, to hold corporate junk bonds over Treasuries.
Meanwhile, average spreads for CCC-rated corporate bonds, the lowest-quality tier, have soared +400 basis points since January, to 968 basis points, their highest since November 2023.
US credit market stress is intensifying.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: History points to stronger equity returns ahead: Since 1928, the S&P 500 has risen +2.1% on average...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
History points to stronger equity returns ahead:
Since 1928, the S&P 500 has risen +2.1% on average during the first half of October in US midterm election years, making it the strongest-performing half-month of Q4.
Over this period, positive returns occurred 71% of the time, the 3rd-best hit rate of the last quarter of the year.
This follows a historically weak second half of September, which has seen a -1.1% decline on average.
Subsequently, in the second half of October, the S&P 500's average return is +0.3%, with a 62% hit rate.
November has historically been even stronger, with the first half averaging a +1.7% return and posting positive returns 79% of the time.
Seasonality is turning more favorable for stocks.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: The US goods trade deficit widened by -$13.7 billion, or +11.5%, in August, to -$132.6 bi...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US goods trade deficit widened by -$13.7 billion, or +11.5%, in August, to -$132.6 billion, its widest gap since March 2025.
US goods imports surged +$17.4 billion, +5.5%, to $336.1 billion, the highest since March 2025.
This was driven by a +16.6% increase in imports of industrial supplies, including petroleum products.
Imports of capital goods, which include computers and accessories, semiconductors, and telecommunications equipment, also increased, reflecting continued demand for AI-related equipment.
At the same time, US goods exports rose +$3.7 billion, or +1.9%, to $203.4 billion, supported by larger shipments of industrial supplies.
The US trade deficit is widening as the Iran War boosts demand for petroleum products, while American companies stockpile goods and materials to mitigate supply-chain disruptions.

item.title: @wallstengine: Nebius $NBIS has acquired Inferize, an AI inference optimization startup, with terms undisclosed. I...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Nebius $NBIS has acquired Inferize, an AI inference optimization startup, with terms undisclosed.
Inferize’s technology is designed to reduce model “cold starts,” cutting the time GPUs sit idle while models load and new capacity spins up.
Nebius will integrate the technology and team into its Token Factory inference platform, aiming to improve GPU utilization, lower inference costs and serve more AI demand from the same infrastructure.

Nebius $NBIS has acquired Inferize, an AI inference optimization startup, with terms undisclosed.

Inferize’s technology is designed to reduce model “cold starts,” cutting the time GPUs sit idle while models load and new capacity spins up.

Nebius will integrate the technology and team into its Token Factory inference platform, aiming to improve GPU utilization, lower inference costs and serve more AI demand from the same infrastructure.

item.title: @wallstengine: U.S. 🇺🇸 employers announced 43,281 job cuts in September, down 18% MoM and 20% YoY, the lowest Se...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
U.S. 🇺🇸 employers announced 43,281 job cuts in September, down 18% MoM and 20% YoY, the lowest September total since 2022.
Q3 cuts also fell 43% from Q2.
But hiring plans remain weak.
Employers announced 90,787 planned hires in September, down 23% YoY and the lowest September total since 2011, with the usual seasonal hiring surge notably muted.
Tech was the outlier: 10,799 cuts, up 77% from August.
AI was cited in 3,961 September cuts and 120,136 year-to-date, around 21% of all announced cuts in 2026.
Source: Challenger, Gray & Christmas.

item.title: @wallstengine: Broadcom $AVGO has agreed to provide Anthropic with up to $42B in financing tied to its AI infrastr...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Broadcom $AVGO has agreed to provide Anthropic with up to $42B in financing tied to its AI infrastructure buildout.
The facility could cover roughly one-third of Anthropic’s $125.2B five-year TPU compute commitment, and the debt may be convertible into Anthropic shares.
Anthropic is also expected to become Broadcom’s largest compute customer in 2027.
The filing says Broadcom’s combined role as hardware supplier and financing partner creates potential conflicts around pricing and access to compute.
Source: Anthropic’s IPO prospectus seen by Reuters

item.title: @wallstengine: $AMZN PLANS TO EXPAND ITS DELIVERY NETWORK TO NEARLY EVERY U.S. ZIP CODE BY 2029 Amazon aims to gro...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$AMZN PLANS TO EXPAND ITS DELIVERY NETWORK TO NEARLY EVERY U.S. ZIP CODE BY 2029
Amazon aims to grow its own delivery network from about 23,700 U.S. ZIP codes today to roughly 39,400 by 2029, according to an internal planning document reviewed by Business Insider.
That would cover about 95% of U.S. ZIP codes and 99.9% of customer demand.
The plan includes 165 new delivery stations from 2027-2029 and about 4,500 additional ZIP codes through Amazon’s rural Hub Delivery program.
The expansion began as part of Project Aurelian, a contingency plan created when Amazon’s USPS contract negotiations became uncertain.
Amazon says the projections are preliminary and could change.

item.title: @wallstengine: $ORCL SIGNS $7B AI COMPUTE DEAL WITH TENCENT Oracle has reportedly signed a five-year deal with Ten...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$ORCL SIGNS $7B AI COMPUTE DEAL WITH TENCENT
Oracle has reportedly signed a five-year deal with Tencent to provide access to roughly 100,000 advanced AI chips across Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia.
The agreement is estimated at about $7B, with roughly 30% paid upfront.
Tencent is using the capacity to train AI models and build agentic products as it ramps investment in AI infrastructure.
The spending is already showing up in its financials:
Q2 infrastructure capex: $7.9B, +176% YoY Q2 free cash flow: -$2B, its first negative quarter in more than a decade
Tencent is also rolling out AI agents across WeChat and its enterprise products.
Source: FT

item.title: @wallstengine: $DELL SIGNS MOU WITH JERA, RHAELM FOR $15B+ JAPAN AI INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT Dell, JERA and RHAELM p...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$DELL SIGNS MOU WITH JERA, RHAELM FOR $15B+ JAPAN AI INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT
Dell, JERA and RHAELM plan to build a standardized model for large-scale AI infrastructure in Japan, starting with a 400 MW project in Chiba.
The first site is expected to exceed $15B in total investment across land, power, construction and AI compute.
JERA will provide behind-the-meter power from its existing plant, RHAELM will develop and operate the site, and Dell will supply the rack-scale AI infrastructure.
Apollo $APO intends to serve as RHAELM’s strategic financing partner.
Operations are targeted to begin in phases in 2028 and reach the full 400 MW in 2029.
The partners are also exploring additional JERA sites, with a broader goal of building multi-gigawatt AI capacity across Japan. The FT estimates the wider infrastructure push could reach roughly $140B.

item.title: @wallstengine: JAPAN 🇯🇵 PLANS $140B AI DATA CENTER PUSH WITH DELL & JERA Japan is planning a major AI infrastruc...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
JAPAN 🇯🇵 PLANS $140B AI DATA CENTER PUSH WITH DELL & JERA
Japan is planning a major AI infrastructure buildout aimed at becoming the largest AI compute hub outside the U.S. and China, according to the FT.
Dell, Jera and Rhaelm have agreed to develop a $15B, 400 MW AI data center near Tokyo, financed by Apollo and expected to begin operations around 2028.
Jera says the group is targeting 3 to 4 GW of AI data center and gas-power infrastructure over the next five years.
At an estimated $35B to $45B per GW, that implies roughly $140B of total investment.
The first Chiba project will not connect to the grid, with dedicated gas-fired generation built alongside the data center to speed up power availability.
For context, current data center power consumption is roughly:
U.S.: 29.2 GW China: 8.5 GW Japan: 1.7 GW
Japan is separately targeting about $206B of public-private investment in cloud and data center infrastructure by 2035.
Source: FT

Dell, Jera and Rhaelm have agreed to develop a $15B, 400 MW AI data center near Tokyo, financed by Apollo and expected to begin operations around 2028.

Jera says the group is targeting 3 to 4 GW of AI data center and gas-power infrastructure over the next five years.

At an estimated $35B to $45B per GW, that implies roughly $140B of total investment.

The first Chiba project will not connect to the grid, with dedicated gas-fired generation built alongside the data center to speed up power availability.

China: 8.5 GW
Japan: 1.7 GW

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Treasury seasonality points to further weakness ahead: The median monthly return on Treasuries duri...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Treasury seasonality points to further weakness ahead:
The median monthly return on Treasuries during October was -0.71% between 2016 and 2025, the 2nd-worst monthly performance of the year.
This is only behind September’s median return of -0.86% over this period.
By comparison, November recorded the strongest median monthly return at +0.69%.
Meanwhile, the 10Y Treasury Note futures are down -2.85% so far this month, on track for their worst September performance since 2022.
At the same time, global government bonds are down -2.1%, putting them on track for their worst September performance since 2023.
History says Treasuries are likely to face more pressure.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: US equity and bond market volatility are moving in opposite directions: The Volatility Index, $VIX,...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
US equity and bond market volatility are moving in opposite directions:
The Volatility Index, $VIX, to MOVE Index ratio is down to 0.15, its lowest since December 2014.
This ratio has fallen -31.5% over the last 2 weeks as the Treasury market volatility intensified.
Over this period, the MOVE Index has surged +25.9 points, or +32.1%, to 106.6, its highest since March 31st.
At the same time, $VIX has declined -1.7 points, or -9.5%, to 16.0, well below its 2026 average of 18.3.
To put this into perspective, during the March to April 2025 correction and the March 2026 pullback, this ratio jumped to 0.37 and 0.36, respectively, as equity volatility followed the surge in bond volatility.
Is stock market volatility set to follow again this time?

item.title: @wallstengine: $SNPS & OPENAI PARTNER ON GPT-SYNOPSYS FOR CHIP DESIGN Synopsys and OpenAI signed a multi-year deal...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$SNPS & OPENAI PARTNER ON GPT-SYNOPSYS FOR CHIP DESIGN
Synopsys and OpenAI signed a multi-year deal to build GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model that can directly use Synopsys EDA tools for semiconductor design.
The model is being designed to handle tasks like PPA optimization, timing closure and verification, with agents running the tools, interpreting results and iterating on designs for engineer review.
OpenAI will license Synopsys’ EDA tools, while both companies will share revenue and jointly take the product to market.
GPT-Synopsys will run on OpenAI-hosted infrastructure and integrate with Synopsys AI and Synopsys Autopilot.
Early customer engagements are already underway.

item.title: @wallstengine: President Trump and leaders from Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and NVIDIA signed the White H...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
President Trump and leaders from Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and NVIDIA signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a voluntary framework for advanced AI safety.
The companies committed to 4 layers of oversight:
• Internal controls to monitor model capabilities & risks • Dedicated internal teams to oversee those controls • Independent external audits • Independent board-level oversight
The companies also agreed to meet regularly to develop common safety standards and best practices.
The accord is voluntary today, but explicitly says some of these measures could eventually be written into law or regulation.
item.content:encoded:
President Trump and leaders from Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and NVIDIA signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a voluntary framework for advanced AI safety.

The companies committed to 4 layers of oversight:

• Internal controls to monitor model capabilities & risks
• Dedicated internal teams to oversee those controls
• Independent external audits
• Independent board-level oversight

The companies also agreed to meet regularly to develop common safety standards and best practices.

The accord is voluntary today, but explicitly says some of these measures could eventually be written into law or regulation.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: We are bullish on humans. ~71% of consumers say they would question a human influencer's recommenda...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
We are bullish on humans.
~71% of consumers say they would question a human influencer's recommendation if they found out AI was used to create the content.
~45% say they would not knowingly trust or engage with an AI influencer at all.
And, ~90% of consumers now expect brands and creators to disclose when content is AI-generated.
The reality is that in the age of AI, human-generated work and content is becoming increasingly rare, but humans value it even more than they did before.
This is exactly why the brands winning right now are investing in real humans, at scale.
AI is great for efficiency, but it cannot replace all human input and generate the same results.

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI SAYS KIMI-LINKED USERS TRIED TO DISTILL ITS MODELS OpenAI says it disrupted a coordinated ca...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI SAYS KIMI-LINKED USERS TRIED TO DISTILL ITS MODELS
OpenAI says it disrupted a coordinated campaign aimed at extracting protected reasoning from its models, with a core cluster linked to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi.
The activity began July 1 and spiked to around 16,000 extraction attempts across 4,000+ users on July 24-25.
OpenAI later identified related activity across a broader cluster of more than 15,000 users.
One method involved taking encrypted reasoning from one conversation and asking another model to decrypt and reproduce it.
OpenAI says there was no breach of its databases, encryption or stored user conversations.
The company banned or restricted accounts, closed the extraction pathway and shared its findings with industry and government partners.
OpenAI says the figures represent attempted extractions, not necessarily successful ones.
item.content:encoded:
OPENAI SAYS KIMI-LINKED USERS TRIED TO DISTILL ITS MODELS

OpenAI says it disrupted a coordinated campaign aimed at extracting protected reasoning from its models, with a core cluster linked to individuals associated with Moonshot AI, the developer of Kimi.

The activity began July 1 and spiked to around 16,000 extraction attempts across 4,000+ users on July 24-25.

OpenAI later identified related activity across a broader cluster of more than 15,000 users.

One method involved taking encrypted reasoning from one conversation and asking another model to decrypt and reproduce it.

OpenAI says there was no breach of its databases, encryption or stored user conversations.

The company banned or restricted accounts, closed the extraction pathway and shared its findings with industry and government partners.

OpenAI says the figures represent attempted extractions, not necessarily successful ones.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Hedge funds sold US equities last week for the first time in 3 weeks. This was driven by...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Hedge funds sold US equities last week for the first time in 3 weeks.
This was driven by macro products, including indexes and ETFs, which accounted for 57% of total sales, with long sales outpacing short covers 1.9 to 1.
Single stocks accounted for the remaining 43%, with short sales outpacing long buys by 1.5 to 1, while short sales were the largest in 3 months.
7 of 11 US sectors were sold, led by Communication Services, Health Care, Energy, and Consumer Staples.
Hedge funds have now sold Health Care stocks for 6 consecutive weeks, the longest sale streak over the last 10 years.
Hedge funds are cutting equity exposure as yields soar.

item.title: @Hedgeye: Here's what most people miss: the range starts breaking before the chart does. The top end stops ma...

item.description:
Here's what most people miss: the range starts breaking before the chart does.
The top end stops making higher highs.
The low end quietly steps up to meet it.
The range narrows.
Nothing looks wrong on the price chart yet - but the character of the move has already changed.
Watch the boundaries, not just the last tick.
That's where a phase transition tells on itself first.

item.title: @wallstengine: ELEVENLABS VALUATION DOUBLES TO $22B AI voice startup ElevenLabs is now valued at $22B after existi...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
ELEVENLABS VALUATION DOUBLES TO $22B
AI voice startup ElevenLabs is now valued at $22B after existing investors and employees sold $300M of stock in a secondary deal led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price.
That’s double its valuation from February, when ElevenLabs raised $500M.
The company says it now has more than 800 employees across 20 countries and counts Deutsche Telekom, Stripe, Revolut, Klarna and the governments of Ukraine and Greece among its customers.
ElevenLabs also develops and trains its own models rather than relying on OpenAI, Google or Anthropic.
The company says it wants to be IPO-ready within the next 2 to 2.5 years.
NVIDIA became a strategic investor in ElevenLabs in 2025.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: US job openings dropped -256,000 in August, to 7.08 million, their lowest level since Mar...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: US job openings dropped -256,000 in August, to 7.08 million, their lowest level since March.
Available vacancies have now declined by -506,000 since April.
The decline was driven by real estate and rental and leasing job openings, which fell -62,000, to 47,000, their lowest since September 2015.
Since January 2025, job openings in this sector have plunged -144,000.
Furthermore, job openings in manufacturing and construction declined -54,000 and -48,000 last month, respectively.
As a result, there are just 48,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, down from 419,000 in July.
The Fed cannot ignore the weak US labor market.
item.content:encoded:
BREAKING: US job openings dropped -256,000 in August, to 7.08 million, their lowest level since March.

Available vacancies have now declined by -506,000 since April.

The decline was driven by real estate and rental and leasing job openings, which fell -62,000, to 47,000, their lowest since September 2015.

Since January 2025, job openings in this sector have plunged -144,000.

Furthermore, job openings in manufacturing and construction declined -54,000 and -48,000 last month, respectively.

As a result, there are just 48,000 more available vacancies than unemployed workers, down from 419,000 in July.

The Fed cannot ignore the weak US labor market.

item.title: @wallstengine: DOORDASH JUST ANNOUNCED A BUNCH OF NEW FEATURES You can now text DoorDash to order food, ask for re...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
DOORDASH JUST ANNOUNCED A BUNCH OF NEW FEATURES
You can now text DoorDash to order food, ask for recommendations or even say “order my usual,” with its AI handling the search, cart and checkout. The beta waitlist is opening for U.S. iPhone users.
Also unveiled DoorDash Air, its own autonomous delivery drone system. Pilots will start in Northern California with Chipotle and Popeyes.
DoorDash says about 80% of typical restaurant orders are small enough for the aircraft, with initial tests averaging under 5 minutes from restaurant to doorstep.
Retail is expanding too, with Macy’s, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland joining the marketplace. DoorDash is also rolling out returns, where a Dasher can pick up eligible items from your home and take them back to the store.
For businesses, DoorDash launched DashOS to connect ordering, reservations, loyalty, guest management and marketing in one system, plus an MCP connector that lets companies bring DoorDash ordering into workplace AI tools.
And for Dashers, it launched DashBuddy, an AI assistant for questions around scheduling, hotspots, payments and other parts of dashing.
item.content:encoded:
DOORDASH JUST ANNOUNCED A BUNCH OF NEW FEATURES

You can now text DoorDash to order food, ask for recommendations or even say “order my usual,” with its AI handling the search, cart and checkout. The beta waitlist is opening for U.S. iPhone users.

Also unveiled DoorDash Air, its own autonomous delivery drone system. Pilots will start in Northern California with Chipotle and Popeyes.

DoorDash says about 80% of typical restaurant orders are small enough for the aircraft, with initial tests averaging under 5 minutes from restaurant to doorstep.

Retail is expanding too, with Macy’s, Anthropologie, The North Face, Vans and Timberland joining the marketplace. DoorDash is also rolling out returns, where a Dasher can pick up eligible items from your home and take them back to the store.

For businesses, DoorDash launched DashOS to connect ordering, reservations, loyalty, guest management and marketing in one system, plus an MCP connector that lets companies bring DoorDash ordering into workplace AI tools.

And for Dashers, it launched DashBuddy, an AI assistant for questions around scheduling, hotspots, payments and other parts of dashing.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Tokenized equities are breaking records, and we are still early. The total market cap of onchain to...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Tokenized equities are breaking records, and we are still early.
The total market cap of onchain tokenized stocks is now up to a record $3.5 billion.
That marks another +33% increase in this month and +860% growth year-over-year.
Growth has accelerated after the SEC's recent Innovation Exemption was announced.
This grants onchain platforms a 5-year "sandbox period" to legally trade tokenized versions of real US stocks.
As a result, Jupiter, the largest onchain platform which is leading the push into tokenized assets, has seen a +104% surge in tokenized equity trading volume this month.
The push toward tokenization is in full-swing.

item.title: @wallstengine: TRUMP EXPECTED TO UNVEIL MAJOR SOUTH KOREAN U.S. ENERGY INVESTMENTS President Trump is expected to...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
TRUMP EXPECTED TO UNVEIL MAJOR SOUTH KOREAN U.S. ENERGY INVESTMENTS
President Trump is expected to announce plans tied to South Korea’s $350B U.S. investment package, including about $54B for the Alaska LNG project and other infrastructure, according to Reuters.
The broader package includes $150B already earmarked for shipbuilding and another $200B for strategic investments.
Among the projects being discussed:
• Up to 8 large nuclear reactors in the U.S., with 6 Westinghouse AP1000 units and 2 South Korean APR1400 reactors. At roughly $15B per reactor, nuclear could account for a large portion of the package.
• A potential South Korean stake in Westinghouse, with discussions around a 5% to 10% holding.
• More than $20B for a 6+ GW gas-fired power project in Texas designed to supply AI data centers and semiconductor facilities.
• Roughly $54B toward Alaska LNG and other U.S. projects. The LNG project would include an 800-mile pipeline from Alaska’s North Slope to an export terminal serving Asian markets.
Important distinction: Reuters says the nuclear projects are still under discussion, so it is not yet confirmed that all eight reactors will be included in Trump’s announcement.

item.title: @wallstengine: Citi downgraded $MRNA to Sell from Neutral, saying the stock’s 222% rally since interim INTerpath-0...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Citi downgraded $MRNA to Sell from Neutral, saying the stock’s 222% rally since interim INTerpath-001 cancer trial results has pushed the valuation too far.
The bank raised its price target to $80 from $60, but says Moderna’s roughly $80B market cap now implies success across multiple cancer indications.
Citi estimates that even assuming 100% success for intismeran’s lead programs, its valuation supports only around $100/share.
To justify roughly $200/share, Citi says the drug would need to generate about $26B in annual cancer sales, nearly 7x its current forecast.
Citi still sees intismeran as potentially becoming a leading melanoma treatment, but says investors now need to see strong efficacy and consistency across patient groups.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: The market will heavily discount today's PCE inflation data. Why? Because the US just changed the w...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
The market will heavily discount today's PCE inflation data.
Why? Because the US just changed the way PCE inflation is calculated:
Beginning with today’s release, the US changed the methodology for 3 key PCE inflation categories and revised data back to 2021:
1. Portfolio management/investment advice 2. Computer software/accessories 3. Legal services
The biggest change is in portfolio management fees. Under the old methodology, rising asset values could show up partly as higher "prices" for portfolio management services.
For example, if an adviser charged 1% of assets and the portfolio rose 20%, the dollar fee would rise 20% even though the adviser did not raise the 1% fee.
The new methodology uses an employment-based measure to estimate the quantity of services, reducing the amount of the increase that is classified as inflation.
For software, the US now uses a broader composite. For legal services, an unpublished CPI series is being replaced because it had become "unusually volatile."
We estimate the methodology alone could reduce Core PCE inflation by up to 20 basis points.
In the PCE inflation data released just now, both headline and Core PCE inflation were revised down by 30 basis points for July.
We do not interpret the entire 30 basis point drop as disinflation.
Part of it is literally a measurement change.

For example, if an adviser charged 1% of assets and the portfolio rose 20%, the dollar fee would rise 20% even though the adviser did not raise the 1% fee.

The new methodology uses an employment-based measure to estimate the quantity of services, reducing the amount of the increase that is classified as inflation.

For software, the US now uses a broader composite. For legal services, an unpublished CPI series is being replaced because it had become "unusually volatile."

In the PCE inflation data released just now, both headline and Core PCE inflation were revised down by 30 basis points for July.

October rate hike odds are falling again.

item.title: @wallstengine: Aterio says Oracle’s $ORCL 1.3 GW Port Washington data center faces a material risk of missing its...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Aterio says Oracle’s $ORCL 1.3 GW Port Washington data center faces a material risk of missing its H2 2027 delivery target because the required grid interconnection is still awaiting regulatory approval.
Aterio’s base case is: Partial power: Dec. 2027 Full 1.3 GW capacity: Oct. 2028 Customer load ramp: mainly from Q1 2028
Construction itself is progressing, with two of four halls already enclosed.
The main dependency is approval for a new high-voltage connection. Wisconsin regulators restarted that review process in August after revoking the original application’s completeness finding.
The next milestone is a PSC completeness decision expected around Oct. 19.
Source: Aterio

item.title: @wallstengine: MCDONALD’S IS USING AI TO SET MENU PRICES IN THE U.S. $MCD is using AI-powered pricing tools that e...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
MCDONALD’S IS USING AI TO SET MENU PRICES IN THE U.S.
$MCD is using AI-powered pricing tools that estimate how much customers at each restaurant are willing to pay and recommend menu prices.
That means the same item can be priced differently even at nearby locations.
One example cited by Reuters showed a Big Mac priced at $5.69 at one Fresno location and $6.89 at another just two miles away, a 21% difference.
McDonald’s says franchisees still set their own final prices, but the company tracks whether they follow the recommendations and sends updated pricing guidance several times a year.
The company says the system is designed to help franchisees make more informed pricing decisions, not mandate prices.

McDonald’s says franchisees still set their own final prices, but the company tracks whether they follow the recommendations and sends updated pricing guidance several times a year.

The company says the system is designed to help franchisees make more informed pricing decisions, not mandate prices.

item.title: @wallstengine: Apple $AAPL plans to enter the smart-home market on Oct. 13 with a new lineup centered around Siri...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
Apple $AAPL plans to enter the smart-home market on Oct. 13 with a new lineup centered around Siri AI, according to Bloomberg.
The main product is a roughly 6-inch smart-home display that can sit on a counter or mount on a wall.
It’s designed to recognize different household members by voice or face and automatically show personalized messages, calendars, contacts, notes and apps.
Apple sees the hub as a central controller for things like locks, thermostats, FaceTime, music, recipes and other connected devices.
Apple is also expected to unveil:
• A new HomePod mini with faster hardware for Siri AI • A new Apple TV with upgraded processors • A broader smart-home ecosystem around HomeKit and Siri
Further out, Apple is developing a privacy-focused home sensor and a higher-end 9-inch hub with a robotic arm that can rotate the display 360 degrees.
The smart-home push is one of the first major product expansions under new CEO John Ternus.
Source: Bloomberg

item.title: @wallstengine: $META is using its AI data centers to help reduce its federal tax bill, classifying parts of the bu...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
$META is using its AI data centers to help reduce its federal tax bill, classifying parts of the buildout as experimental “pilot models” to claim research tax credits on equipment, including AI chips
Total research tax-credit: 2023: $700M 2024: $2B 2025: $3.9B 2026: $7B, rough estimate
The credits cover both R&D labor and certain equipment costs tied to technical work around data center design and networking large numbers of chips.
These figures include all of Meta’s research tax credits, not just data centers.
Meta’s filings also note that some of these tax positions could be challenged by the IRS.
Source: NYT

item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: The US is officially closing its last major military base in Iraq after spending more than 23 years and $1.7 trillion in the country.
A US defense official said the military is airlifting its last equipment and personnel out of Erbil, the last US base in Iraq.
Some US Marines will remain to protect American "diplomatic missions," along with contractors to maintain Iraq’s fleet of F-16 fighter jets and American-made tanks.
"We don’t think we need the military there anymore," Trump said.

item.description:
$HOOD just unveiled Robinhood Agents, built directly into the app.
You can use one to research the market, build a strategy, and place trades within limits you set.
Each agent only gets access to a dedicated agentic trading account, and manual trade approval is on by default.
Robinhood says 150,000+ customers have already opened agentic trading accounts, with agents now using its tools nearly 30 million times a day.

You can also use OpenAI’s GPT-Luna for free through the end of the year.

This is also the 2nd-lowest reading since the April 2025 "Liberation Day" market sell-off.

On Monday, new 52-week lows on the NYSE outnumbered new highs for the 10th consecutive trading day and in 14 of the last 15 trading sessions.
Market breadth is rapidly deteriorating.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: AI spending is becoming extremely concentrated: The proportion of US software-spending businesses u...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
AI spending is becoming extremely concentrated:
The proportion of US software-spending businesses using paid GPU infrastructure is up to a record ~10%, from less than 4% two years ago.
Model serving and inference, or spending on the computing power needed to run AI models and process AI requests, account for the vast majority of this increase.
The proportion of firms using model serving and inference is up to a record 8.7% from 2.4% over this period.
Meanwhile, the top 10% of firms by spending account for 99.5% of model-serving spending and 99.0% of neocloud spending, or specialized AI cloud services.
The top 10% also represent 95.7% of cloud computing spending and 95.6% of spending on OpenAI and Anthropic.
AI adoption is broadening, but spending remains heavily concentrated.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: Gold prices have rarely been as volatile as they are now. Gold futures have recorded 7 daily declin...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
Gold prices have rarely been as volatile as they are now.
Gold futures have recorded 7 daily declines of -3.5% or more so far this year, the highest count since 2008.
This is already more than double the 3 trading sessions recorded in 2025.
By comparison, the largest annual number of sessions with declines of -3.5% or more was recorded in 1980, at 33.
With 3 months of trading remaining, 2026 is on track to be the most volatile year for gold futures prices since 1982.
As a result, gold futures prices are down -5.4% year-to-date, on track for their first annual drop since 2022, following their best year since 1979.
The bond market has catalyzing some of gold's most volatile conditions in history.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Bitcoin is up +43.1% so far in Q3 2026, on track for its best quarterly performance since...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Bitcoin is up +43.1% so far in Q3 2026, on track for its best quarterly performance since Q4 2024.
This would also mark their 3rd-best quarterly gain since US spot Bitcoin ETFs officially began trading in January 2024.
Since August 19th alone, Bitcoin prices have surged +29.8% when the US Treasury said it would increase buybacks of long-dated Treasuries.
Meanwhile, US spot Bitcoin ETFs posted +$2.4 billion in inflows in the week ending September 25th, their largest weekly intake since October 2025.
As a result, year-to-date inflows are up to +$1.0 billion, from -$5.0 billion in total outflows recorded at the end of July.
Crypto is in a new bull market.

item.title: @Hedgeye: McCullough: The Last Time Yields Did This, I Called the 2008 Crash 🔊 On Tuesday's edition of The M...
item.dc:creator: @Hedgeye
item.description:
McCullough: The Last Time Yields Did This, I Called the 2008 Crash
🔊
On Tuesday's edition of The Macro Show, Hedgeye CEO @KeithMcCullough explained why he is still short long-term bonds at new cycle highs and what the last cycle says about where yields go from here.
The 2-year yield made a new cycle high at 4.95% this morning, moving toward the top of the range at 5.00%, alongside a dollar breakout.
The two signals travel together, and Hedgeye publishes a daily Risk Range™ on both the dollar index and the 2-year.
The Fed is the setup.
The market is pricing in more hikes than it probably should, and the Fed typically goes too far, reacting to late-cycle data on a lag.
Until the bond market is done pricing that in, the short stays on. $TLT has been the vehicle, with $ZROZ on alongside it.
"5.29-ish is where bond yields stopped going up in '07, when I started thinking about this pending market crash of 2008."
What followed was the long cycle.
"It went to 1.39% by 2012."

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI DEV DAY 2026 RECAP: OpenAI just wrapped its biggest DevDay yet, with updates across ChatGPT,...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI DEV DAY 2026 RECAP:
OpenAI just wrapped its biggest DevDay yet, with updates across ChatGPT, agents, models, Codex, plugins and enterprise products.
Here’s the full recap, roughly in order of what matters most:
1. Dots: always-on AI agents
This was probably the biggest product announcement.
Dots are persistent agents inside ChatGPT that can take on ongoing responsibilities, keep working between conversations and use their own cloud computer.
They can work across connected apps, run scheduled tasks and bring results back when they need your input.
Available for Pro and Business Premium, with Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare beta access.
2. GPT-6.1 Sol
OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Sol, a major upgrade to GPT-6 Sol focused on agentic coding, computer use and professional work.
OpenAI says it delivers near-Astra intelligence at one-fifth of Astra’s standard input and output token pricing.
Available across the API and ChatGPT plans including Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu.
3. GPT-6 Astra Ultrafast
OpenAI introduced a premium speed tier for workloads where latency matters.
Astra Ultrafast can generate up to 300 tokens/second in Codex, around 8x faster, and up to 6x faster through the API.
GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast is coming next.
4. ChatGPT is becoming a platform for developers
OpenAI is opening more of the infrastructure it uses to build ChatGPT itself.
Developers can now create Plugin Extensions with their own sidebar presence, interactive interfaces and custom file viewers directly inside ChatGPT.
OpenAI is also improving plugin creation, submission, ranking and discovery.
5. Agents API gets computer use
The Agents API can now power agents that actually interact with software.
It also brings in multi-agent capabilities, tool search, tool calling and context compaction, while OpenAI handles the underlying infrastructure.
Amazon is also launching Bedrock Managed Agents powered by OpenAI, allowing these agents to run natively inside AWS.
6. Codex can now work basically anywhere
Codex can now run on your computer, remotely from your phone or entirely in the cloud.
Reusable cloud development environments let teams give Codex shared setups, permissions and configurations without needing a developer’s laptop running.
Codex also got:
• A redesigned CLI with voice control and multi-agent task management • A new Code Review experience for GitHub and GitLab • Automatic cloud code reviews while you’re away • Codex Security Cloud for scanning repositories, investigating vulnerabilities and preparing fixes
7. ChatGPT Space
OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Space, a shared workspace where teams, ChatGPT and Dots can work together using the same knowledge.
ChatGPT can organize the workspace based on team instructions, while people and agents can continue work from the same context.
Available to Pro, Business and Enterprise users.
8. Pages and collaborative Slides
Pages are new collaborative documents built around humans and AI working together.
Inside a Page, you can write, research, generate charts and images, visualize information and collaborate with other people.
OpenAI is also adding collaborative Slides where multiple people and agents can edit the same deck simultaneously.
Slides can be presented inside ChatGPT or exported to PowerPoint and Google Slides while preserving formatting.
9. Teams can delegate work to ChatGPT
Business and Enterprise users can now create teams and share Pages, Slides, plugins and spreadsheets.
Teams can also delegate recurring work to ChatGPT, such as weekly project updates.
Those tasks can run on a schedule or be triggered by events like a new email or Slack message.
10. ChatGPT comes directly to Slack and Microsoft Teams
Teams can mention @ChatGPT inside channels, threads or DMs.
ChatGPT can use connected company tools and context to answer questions or help with work without everyone needing to move into a separate ChatGPT conversation.
11. Plugins can now trigger automations
OpenAI is adding support for MCP Events.
That means a connected app can trigger ChatGPT automatically when something happens.
Example: a new task appears on a project board, ChatGPT reads the related documents and drafts a plan without waiting for someone to manually ask.
12. Sites can host plugins
Plugins can now be embedded into Sites built with ChatGPT.
Different teammates can use the same application with their own connected data and permissions, while automations can keep shared information updated.
13. Decisions API
OpenAI introduced a new API aimed at fast, structured decisions.
Developers give Luna context plus a predefined set of possible answers, and the model chooses between them.
Potential uses include classification, routing requests and deciding what an agent should do next.
14. Private Intelligence
OpenAI introduced new enterprise privacy infrastructure.
Zero Data Retention with Private Safety Processing allows automated safety checks without OpenAI personnel accessing the underlying content.
OpenAI is also previewing Private Inference, combining confidential computing with verifiable controls, coming this fall.
15. Meetings plugin
ChatGPT can now take meeting notes and save personalized summaries and action items directly into ChatGPT Space.
Those notes can then feed into other work, like updating a project plan or drafting follow-ups.
OpenAI says meeting audio is deleted after the notes are generated.
16. Sign in with ChatGPT
OpenAI is extending ChatGPT subscriptions beyond ChatGPT itself.
Plus and Pro users can use their plan allowance across participating third-party tools.
OpenAI says there are 16 launch partners, including Devin, Notion, Vercel, T3, OpenClaw and Dactyl.
17. New Pro 500 plan
OpenAI launched Pro 500, its highest-usage individual tier.
It offers 25x the ChatGPT Plus usage allowance and includes access to Ultrafast.
18. OpenAI Marketplace
Enterprise customers will be able to apply part of their existing OpenAI commitment toward approved third-party software.
The initial group includes 32 partners, including Adobe, Figma, Salesforce, ServiceNow, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Harvey and others.
19. Shareable profiles
Businesses can create profiles showcasing Sites, plugins and other things they’ve built, making them easier for other people to discover and reuse.
ChatGPT has now reached 1.2 billion weekly users.

item.title: @wallstengine: OPENAI LAUNCHES DOTS, ALWAYS-ON AI AGENTS INSIDE CHATGPT OpenAI is rolling out Dots, a new type of...
item.dc:creator: @wallstengine
item.description:
OPENAI LAUNCHES DOTS, ALWAYS-ON AI AGENTS INSIDE CHATGPT
OpenAI is rolling out Dots, a new type of agent powered by GPT-6 Astra that can keep working for you in the background, even between conversations.
Each Dot gets its own cloud computer and browser, can connect to thousands of apps, remember ongoing context, run scheduled tasks and bring results back for review.
Users can also set rules around what the agent can do automatically versus what needs approval.
OpenAI says Dots can research, review calendars, work across connected apps and continue making progress without needing a new prompt every time.
Dots are starting to roll out to Pro users today, with Business Premium support and an Enterprise beta as well.
OpenAI says usage won’t count against eligible plan allowances for the next month.
Users start with a primary Dot, and OpenAI says the longer-term plan is to let people create entire teams of them.

item.title: @KobeissiLetter: BREAKING: Inventories in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by ~800,000 barrels last week, to...
item.dc:creator: @KobeissiLetter
item.description:
BREAKING: Inventories in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by ~800,000 barrels last week, to 283.8 million barrels, the lowest level since 1982.
This marks the 27th consecutive weekly decline, putting inventories down more than -132 million barrels from their high.
Meanwhile, the Trump Administration is now offering up to 40 million barrels of crude oil from the SPR, which would could drive total inventories below 250 million barrels.
America's oil reserves are running near their lowest levels in history.
